name: Afghanistan
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Afghanistan has no e-invoicing mandate and no credible programme has been announced. The country operates a VAT system at a standard rate of 10 percent, with e-invoicing explicitly described as not mandatory. Monitoring continues for any future developments.

name: Åland Islands
keyDate: B2G mandatory since April 2020 (all public authorities); B2B soft right since April 2021
format: Finvoice 3.0 / TEAPPSXML 3.0 / Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 (all EN 16931-compliant)
authority: Finnish Tax Administration (Verohallinto) and State Treasury (Valtiokonttori) as Peppol Authority
summary: Åland Islands does not operate a separate e-invoicing regime and is administered under Finnish law for tax and invoicing purposes. Finland has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate under Act 241/2019, requiring all suppliers to public authorities to issue EN 16931-compliant structured e-invoices; this obligation has applied to all public bodies since April 2020 and was extended to full EN 16931 compliance for all B2G and qualifying B2B transactions from April 2021. There is no general B2B or B2C mandate, though any Finnish business with annual turnover above EUR 10,000 has a statutory right to demand structured e-invoices from its suppliers. No national ViDA implementing legislation has been published as of the source dates; EU-wide requirements are expected to apply from 1 July 2030.

name: Albania
keyDate: Phased mandatory fiscalisation in 2021 (B2G 1 Jan, B2B 1 Jul, B2C/cash 1 Sep); import fiscalisation window extended to 7 days from January 2026
format: UBL 2.1 XML via the Central Information System (CIS)
authority: General Directorate of Taxes (Drejtoria e Përgjithshme e Tatimeve)
summary: Albania operates a universal real-time fiscalisation system covering B2B, B2G and B2C transactions under Law No. 87/2019, administered through the General Directorate of Taxes' Central Information System (CIS). Invoices are submitted as UBL 2.1 XML, verified in real time, and assigned a unique NIVF identifier plus QR code before they are legally valid. Buyers of services from nonresident suppliers complete a reverse-charge invoice workflow inside the same platform, while imported goods have been subject to a fiscalisation procedure completable within seven days of entry into free circulation since January 2026. A separate 2025 measure requires transport and accommodation businesses to install POS terminals, with the obligation expected to extend to all businesses by end of 2026.

name: Algeria
keyDate: Implementing framework awaited; no confirmed mandate date
summary: Algeria has signalled an intent to introduce electronic invoicing through successive Finance Law deliberations, with the Direction Générale des Impôts identified as the responsible authority. No implementing regulation, confirmed mandate date, technical format, or clearance model has been published in the available sources. A voluntary, collaborative open-standard initiative called e-facture-dz has emerged from the software-editor community to define a JSON-native protocol ahead of any regulatory mandate.

name: American Samoa
keyDate: No mandate
authority: American Samoa Government Tax Office, Department of the Treasury
summary: American Samoa operates its own independent tax administration, modelled on the US Internal Revenue Code as it stood on 31 December 2000, but with distinct territorial provisions administered by the American Samoa Government Tax Office. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, voluntary framework, or credible programme of any kind has been identified in any available official source. The territory remains entirely outside the scope of e-invoicing regulation as of August 2026.

name: Andorra
keyDate: B2G mandatory from Jan 2025 (general administration); communes and other public entities from Jan 2027
format: Electronically signed PDF (transitional); structured e-invoice (phased in)
summary: Andorra has introduced mandatory e-invoicing for suppliers to its general public administration from January 1, 2025, via a dedicated government portal and register launched on October 1, 2024. Communes and other public entities follow on January 1, 2027, after a one-year extension confirmed in December 2025. There is no domestic B2B or B2C e-invoicing mandate, and the Departament de Tributs i de Fronteres has not announced any roadmap for one.

name: Angola
keyDate: Presidential Decree No. 71/25 (20 March 2025) effective mid-September 2025; Phase 1 mandatory 1 January 2026 for large taxpayers (turnover ≥ Kz 350 million), government suppliers, and very-high-value invoices (≥ Kz 25 million); Phase 2 extends to all remaining VAT-registered businesses by 1 January 2027
model: Post-clearance — invoices generated via AGT-certified software, transmitted to AGT for registration then content validation; rejected/invalid invoices are treated as not issued
format: JSON (for AGT data exchange); human-readable versions (e.g. PDF) must include a specified QR code
authority: Administração Geral Tributária (AGT) — General Tax Administration
summary: Angola is implementing a phased mandatory e-invoicing system under Presidential Decree No. 71/25 (20 March 2025), with detailed technical rules set out in Executive Decree 683/25. The Decree became effective mid-September 2025 (six months after publication), followed by a "soft landing" transition period (1 October-31 December 2025) during which businesses could use old invoice formats without penalty while the General Tax Administration (AGT) finalised software certification. Phase 1 became mandatory from 1 January 2026, applying to large taxpayers (annual turnover ≥ Kz 350 million), government suppliers (B2G), and any invoice of very high value (≥ Kz 25 million) regardless of issuer size. Phase 2 runs September 2026-January 2027, extending the mandate to all remaining VAT-registered businesses under the General or Simplified VAT regimes by 1 January 2027. The system operates a post-clearance model: invoices are generated via AGT-certified software in JSON format, transmitted to AGT for registration and then content validation, with rejected or invalid invoices treated as not issued at all.

name: Anguilla
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Anguilla has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or programme of any kind. The territory operates its own Inland Revenue Department, levies no income tax and no VAT, and relies instead on a Goods and Services Tax together with various other indirect levies. No legal instrument introducing e-invoicing has been identified in any official source.

name: Antigua & Barbuda
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Antigua & Barbuda in the sources reviewed. The market-research report forecasts commercial e-invoicing software adoption, not a government mandate — no evidence of an actual legal requirement was found.

name: Argentina
keyDate: Mandatory for all taxpayers; expanded to additional sectors from 1 July 2026
authority: ARCA (Agencia de Recaudación y Control Aduanero, formerly AFIP)
summary: Argentina operates a real-time clearance model under which every invoice must receive an Electronic Authorisation Code (CAE) from ARCA before it has fiscal validity. The mandate covers all taxpayers for B2B, B2C, and B2G transactions. General Resolution 5824/2026, effective 1 July 2026, extends the obligation to sectors previously exempt, including banks, insurers, credit card providers, private educational institutions, and prepaid medical plans, and introduces a monthly electronic settlement statement for high-volume issuers.

name: Armenia
keyDate: Mandatory for all businesses since 2016
summary: Armenia operates a fully live, mandatory electronic invoicing system administered by the State Revenue Committee. E-invoicing has been compulsory for all businesses covering B2G, B2B, and B2C transactions since 2016, following an initial rollout for large taxpayers from 2010. The government-operated platform handles invoice creation, signing, transmission, and compliance validation in real time.

name: Aruba
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Aruba has no e-invoicing mandate, announced programme, or formal proposal as of August 2026. The Departamento di Impuesto (DIMP) launched the second phase of its online tax portal (BOi) in May 2026, representing a significant step toward digital tax administration, but this covers tax assessments, payment plans, and fiscal account management rather than e-invoicing. Aruba operates its own independent tax system based on a cumulative turnover tax (BBO/BAZV/BAVP) rather than a VAT, and no credible e-invoicing initiative has been identified in authoritative sources.

name: Australia
keyDate: B2G receive 30% Peppol by Jul 2026; full send/receive by Dec 2026
summary: Australia operates a voluntary Peppol e-invoicing framework for B2B while progressively mandating Peppol capability across federal government entities. By 1 July 2026, all Non-Corporate Commonwealth Entities must ensure at least 30% of invoices received are Peppol e-invoices, and by December 2026 they must be able to automatically process and send e-invoices using the Peppol standard. No nationwide B2B mandate has been announced or legislated.

name: Austria
keyDate: B2G mandatory since Jan 2014 (federal); extended to all public authorities Apr 2020; no B2B mandate
model: Decentralised via national portals (USP / e-Rechnung.gv.at) and Peppol eDelivery network
summary: Austria mandated e-invoicing for federal government suppliers from 1 January 2014 under the IKT-Konsolidierungsgesetz, extended to all sub-central public authorities by 18 April 2020 in line with EU Directive 2014/55/EU. Invoices must be submitted via the USP portal or e-Rechnung.gv.at in ebInterface or Peppol BIS 3.0 format. B2B and B2C e-invoicing remain entirely voluntary, with no domestic mandate date announced; the EU ViDA package introduces cross-border digital reporting from 1 July 2030.

name: Azerbaijan
keyDate: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses; B2B/B2G since April 2017, extended to all commercial-supply taxpayers 1 January 2018; mandatory non-resident B2C e-service VAT registration from 23 August 2026
format: Local XML (e-qaimə / e-VHF), validated against the STS XSD schema — not EN 16931/Peppol
authority: State Tax Service (STS) under the Ministry of Economy
summary: Azerbaijan operates a fully live mandatory e-invoicing regime for all VAT-registered businesses across B2B and B2G transactions (B2C is out of scope for e-invoices, handled instead by real-time cash registers). Electronic tax invoices, known locally as e-qaimə or e-VHF, must be issued and submitted through the State Tax Service portal at e-taxes.gov.az, authenticated with an enhanced electronic signature (Asan İmza / SIMA Token), and are governed by Tax Code Article 218.1.2 (issuers) and Article 58 (financial sanctions). A VAT deposit-account split-payment mechanism (Cabinet of Ministers Decision No. 219/2007) requires the VAT portion of B2B payments to reach a Treasury-held account within one business day as a condition of input-VAT credit, backed by a 50% penalty for non-compliance. Non-resident B2C e-service providers face mandatory VAT registration from 23 August 2026 but do not issue Azerbaijani e-invoices themselves.

name: Bahamas
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The Bahamas has no e-invoicing or transaction-level continuous transaction control mandate in place, and no such programme has been announced or proposed. The Department of Inland Revenue administers VAT and other taxes through an online portal, but invoicing remains outside any structured digital mandate.

name: Bahrain
keyDate: Phased rollout anticipated from 2026 (large taxpayers first); no confirmed effective date published by the NBR
format: TBC — XML/JSON or UBL-based structured format anticipated
summary: Bahrain's National Bureau for Revenue has confirmed that a B2B e-invoicing mandate is in development, with a phased rollout anticipated to begin in 2026, large taxpayers first. The NBR issued a tender in 2023 for the central e-invoicing platform, ran a business consultation/survey through 2024-2025, and the 2025/26 Budget signalled the mandate alongside other tax reforms including a possible VAT rate increase from the current 10%. One concrete change has already landed: the prior requirement for tax-authority approval before issuing e-invoices has been removed, opening a voluntary runway for businesses that want to exchange structured e-invoices before any mandate takes effect. As of August 2026, no detailed technical specifications, confirmed launch dates, or binding legal instrument have been formally published.

name: Bangladesh
keyDate: Phased rollout ongoing; full mandate date not yet confirmed
summary: Bangladesh's National Board of Revenue is rolling out a national VAT e-invoicing programme under the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012, with a pilot launched in 2023 and phased onboarding progressing through 2024 to 2026. As of mid-2026, binding go-live dates and final technical specifications have not been formally confirmed by the NBR. Sectoral pilots continue to expand, with broader mandatory scope pending formal legislative communication.

name: Barbados
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Barbados in the sources reviewed. Official BRA and government portals confirm general online tax filing and payment infrastructure, but no source describes a structured e-invoicing mandate, format, or platform.

name: Belarus
keyDate: Mandatory VAT e-invoicing via ESCF since 2016
summary: Belarus operates a clearance-based e-invoicing system for VAT transactions through the national Electronic System of Invoices (ESCF). Invoices must be submitted to the Ministry of Taxes and Duties portal for approval before delivery to the recipient. The format is a national XML standard administered by NALOG.

name: Belgium
keyDate: Mandatory B2B from 1 Jan 2026
summary: Structured B2B e-invoicing via the Peppol network became mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses established in Belgium on 1 January 2026, following legislation published in the Belgian Official Gazette on 20 February 2024. Invoices must comply with EN 16931, with Peppol BIS 3.0 as the default format, though other EN 16931-compliant formats are permitted by mutual agreement. A near-real-time e-reporting layer using a Peppol 5-corner model is planned for January 2028, and cross-border intra-EU B2B e-invoicing is expected to follow in January 2030 under the EU ViDA initiative.

name: Belize
keyDate: Mandatory for large taxpayers from 2027 (exact date TBC)
summary: Belize has enacted the General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2024, which took effect on 1 January 2025 and provides the legal foundation for mandatory e-invoicing under a centralised pre-clearance model. The Belize Tax Service Department is managing the rollout with IDB and CIAT support, targeting large taxpayers from 2027, though detailed technical specifications and the phased implementation schedule have not yet been published. The mandate will require all GST-registered entities to issue and report invoices electronically through BTSD authorisation before documents are valid for tax purposes.

name: Benin
keyDate: MECeF / e-MECeF mandatory since 2020, DGI-administered; PAG II Program (2021-2026) extending coverage to new sectors
model: Clearance — invoice sent to DGI's e-MECeF platform for real-time validation, assigned a QR code and unique number (NIM) before it is legally valid and can be shared with the customer
summary: Benin mandates electronic invoicing under the "Facture Normalisée" (Standardized Invoice) regime, introduced in 2020 and administered by the Directorate General of Taxes (DGI). Invoices are issued via the MECeF (physical certified billing machine) or e-MECeF (its software counterpart) and validated in real time by the DGI, which assigns a unique number (NIM) and QR code before the invoice becomes legally valid. The mandate primarily covers B2B and B2G transactions, requires 10-year archiving, and is being extended to new sectors under the government's PAG II digitalisation programme (2021-2026).

name: Bermuda
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner (OTC), Bermuda
summary: Bermuda has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme of any kind. The Office of the Tax Commissioner administers a range of taxes including payroll tax, land tax, and corporate services tax, and operates an online E-Tax payment and filing tool, but none of these involve e-invoicing obligations. Bermuda has no VAT and no goods-and-services tax, removing the principal regulatory driver that typically motivates e-invoicing mandates.

name: Bhutan
keyDate: E-invoicing law effective 1 January 2026; full rollout scope TBC
summary: Bhutan enacted the Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Act 2025, effective 1 January 2026, which replaced the 7% sales tax with a 5% GST and revised exemptions. The Department of Revenue and Customs has issued guidelines for e-invoicing implementation and the GovTech Agency has published a list of GST-compliant invoicing solution providers, indicating an active rollout. However, the precise model, technical format, mandate scope and phasing dates are not confirmed in the available sources.

name: Bolivia
keyDate: Groups 9–12 mandatory from October 2026; earlier groups already live
summary: Bolivia operates a phased mandatory e-invoicing regime under the Virtual Invoicing System (SFV), administered by the National Tax Service (SIN). Large taxpayers have been live since December 2021, with eight further waves bringing additional groups online through October 2024. Taxpayer groups 9 through 12, comprising 27,973 taxpayers, had their compliance deadline extended to October 1, 2026 via Resolution No. 102600000007 published on 23 March 2026.

name: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius & Saba
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba (the BES islands) operate under a distinct tax regime administered by Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland (BCN), a dedicated Caribbean Netherlands division of the Dutch Tax and Customs Administration. The principal indirect tax is the General Expenditure Tax (GET), not VAT, and EU law does not automatically apply to these territories. No e-invoicing mandate, pilot, platform, or credible programme has been identified in any available official or authoritative source.

name: Bosnia & Herzegovina
keyDate: FBiH law effective no later than 31 Aug 2027; B2C within 2 years, B2B/B2G within 3 years of entry into force
authority: Federal Ministry of Finance / Indirect Taxation Authority (ITA)
summary: The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH) adopted the Law on Transaction Fiscalization, published 4 February 2026, mandating real-time electronic invoicing and reporting for B2B, B2G, and B2C transactions via a Central Platform for Fiscalisation. The law must take full effect no later than 31 August 2027, with a phased rollout over two to three years from entry into force. Republika Srpska and Brcko District operate under separate frameworks; no single national mandate exists across all three jurisdictions.

name: Botswana
keyDate: Three-year pilot programme ran 2022-March 2025; Electronic VAT Invoicing Solution (Electronic Fiscal Devices, EFDs) announced in the February 2025 Budget Speech for mandatory rollout to all VAT-registered businesses from March 2026
model: Continuous Transaction Control — Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs) or approved software record every sale and share transaction data directly with the Botswana Unified Revenue Service (BURS)
format: Not yet published — technical specifications, exact platform, and integration model still pending as of the sources reviewed
summary: Botswana is rolling out mandatory electronic VAT invoicing via Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs), following a three-year pilot programme that ran from 2022 to March 2025. The Minister of Finance announced the nationwide rollout in the 2025/26 Budget Speech (February 2025), with mandatory e-invoicing for all VAT-registered businesses set to commence in March 2026. The system operates as a Continuous Transaction Control (CTC) model: EFDs — devices or approved software that record every sale and generate a verifiable receipt with a unique identifier — share transaction data directly with the Botswana Unified Revenue Service (BURS) in real time, enabling continuous transaction monitoring rather than periodic post-filing review. As of the sources reviewed, Botswana authorities had not yet released full technical specifications (exact platform, format, or integration model), though the rollout will likely begin with VAT-registered businesses per international practice and Botswana's VAT Amendment Act, with smaller non-VAT businesses potentially phased in later or exempted.

name: Brazil
keyDate: NF-e/NFS-e clearance mature and universal; CBS/IBS consumption-tax reform transition year 2026 (temporary rates 0.9%/0.1%), new e-invoice/XML requirements expected around August 2026, most obligations phasing through the reform's multi-year timetable, some individual/rural-producer CBS duties delayed to 1 Jan 2027
format: NF-e / NFS-e / NFCom XML; new IBS/CBS-layer XML requirements expected around August 2026
summary: Brazil's NF-e (goods) and NFS-e (services) clearance-model e-invoicing is mature and effectively universal, with SEFAZ validating invoices before legal issuance. NFCom was separately introduced as a mandatory e-invoicing requirement for telecom-sector transactions. The bigger current story is Brazil's CBS/IBS dual-VAT consumption tax reform: 2026 is a transition year using temporary token rates (CBS 0.9%, IBS 0.1%) while the real rates and full implementation timetable are finalised, and new e-invoice/XML requirements tied to the reform are expected around August 2026. A narrow delay pushes some CBS registration and invoicing duties for individuals and rural producers to 1 January 2027, but this does not affect the broader reform timeline for companies, legal entities, foreign businesses or non-resident digital service providers.

name: British Virgin Islands
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The British Virgin Islands has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme. The territory's tax base consists of payroll tax, stamp duty, property tax, and similar levies but no VAT or general sales tax, leaving no structural foundation on which an e-invoicing obligation could be built. The Inland Revenue Department, operating under the BVI Ministry of Finance, administers these taxes but has published no e-invoicing initiative.

name: Brunei
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed; Brunei's Treasury Accounting and Financial Information System (TAFIS 2.0) includes an invoice-status-viewing feature for government financial processes, but this is not confirmed to be a structured e-invoicing or CTC system
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Brunei in the sources reviewed, despite the country's prior 'proposed'-adjacent classification research context (existing status recorded as 'none'). Brunei operates TAFIS (Treasury Accounting and Financial Information System, now on version 2.0, built on SAP), the government's core financial management system, which includes a feature to "VIEW INVOICE STATUS" — but the banked sources describe only system maintenance/downtime notices for TAFIS, with no substantive description of its invoicing functionality, no confirmation it constitutes structured e-invoicing, and no indication it extends to private-sector B2B transactions. Brunei is a member of ASEAN, a regional bloc where, per one industry source, e-invoicing implementation is generally described as being "in its initial phase" continent-wide, with only Singapore and Indonesia cited as having live mandates as of that source's review, and Brunei not mentioned among the five countries "planning to introduce it in the nearest time."

name: Bulgaria
keyDate: SAF-T large taxpayers from Jan 2026; B2B mandate under consultation; on-demand SAF-T requests from 1 Jul 2026
model: Post-audit (current); Clearance model under consultation for B2B
format: EN 16931 / UBL 2.1 (B2G); SAF-T BG (reporting); B2B format TBC
authority: NRA (National Revenue Agency); Ministry of Transport, Information Technology and Communications
summary: Bulgaria has no mandatory B2G, B2B, or B2C e-invoicing requirement for suppliers, though all public contracting authorities must receive and process EN 16931-compliant e-invoices since 1 November 2019. The National Revenue Agency is introducing phased SAF-T reporting obligations beginning with large taxpayers on 1 January 2026, with full rollout expected by 2030. A public consultation on a mandatory clearance-model B2B e-invoicing regime is underway, but no binding mandate or implementation date has yet been legislated.

name: Burkina Faso
keyDate: Certified Electronic Invoice (FEC) system officially launched 6 January 2026; mandatory for Phase 1 (domestic RNI taxpayers with annual turnover ≥ XOF 50 million) from 1 July 2026; subsequent phases TBD
model: Clearance — invoices issued through certified software (proprietary or third-party) connected to the SECeF platform, with real-time data transmission and QR-code verification
format: FEC — Facture Électronique Certifiée (structured electronic format)
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
summary: Burkina Faso officially launched the Certified Electronic Invoice (Facture Électronique Certifiée, FEC) system on 6 January 2026, transitioning from its 2017 standardised-invoice framework to a real-time Continuous Transaction Control model via the SECeF platform (Système Électronique de Certification de la Facturation). The 2025 Finance Law and Ministerial Order 2025-0047/MEF/SG/DGI provide the legal foundation. Phase 1 applies to domestic companies under the standard tax regime (RNI) with annual turnover excluding tax of at least XOF 50 million (~EUR 76,200), mandatory from 1 July 2026, covering both B2B and B2C domestic VAT transactions; non-resident VAT-registered businesses, foreign companies without permanent establishment, non-commercial government invoicing, air traffic, and urban public passenger transport are excluded. Penalties under the General Tax Code are severe: 5 times the compromised VAT (minimum XOF 500,000) for a first offence, rising to 10 times (minimum XOF 1,000,000) for repeat offences.

name: Burundi
keyDate: EBMS mandatory since January 2022 for certain taxpayers; second phase launched 18 March 2025 (5,000 additional fiscal devices, total ~8,000, use now described as mandatory for traders)
model: Fiscal devices — real-time transmission of invoice data to OBR via the Electronic Billing Management System (EBMS)
summary: Burundi introduced the Electronic Billing Management System (EBMS) in January 2022, requiring certain taxpayers — including domestic and foreign providers of digitalised services — to submit invoice data in real time to the Office Burundais des Recettes (OBR). The system launched with over 200 taxpayers connected and has since expanded: a March 2025 second phase added 5,000 fiscal invoicing devices (on top of 3,000 already deployed), with OBR now describing device collection and use as mandatory for traders and warning of sanctions for non-compliance. Implementation has faced acknowledged challenges, and the system is still described as being in an adaptation phase.

name: Cambodia
keyDate: CamInvoice soft-launched 12 December 2024; Phase 1 B2G mandatory rollout completed across 14+ ministries by end of 2025; B2B remains voluntary in 2025-2026, mandatory for a defined group of large/high-risk taxpayers expected 2026-2027; B2C anticipated 2027+
model: Clearance — invoice data submitted in UBL XML to the CamInvoice platform for real-time validation; only after a unique QR code is returned is the invoice legally valid
authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT), tax administration; General Department of Digital Economy (GDDE), technical operations
summary: Cambodia is rolling out a national e-invoicing platform, CamInvoice (CamInv), under a phased mandate initiated with a soft launch on 12 December 2024 and officially launched 12 May 2025 (Prakas No. 075 MEF). The General Department of Digital Economy (GDDE) operates the technical platform, with blockchain-based storage via CamDL, while the General Department of Taxation (GDT) handles tax administration. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory, extended step by step through 2025 to cover 14+ central government ministries (Circulars 003 and 012). B2B remains voluntary through 2025-2026 but a phased mandatory rollout for a defined group of taxpayers — likely large or high-risk businesses — is expected in 2026-2027, with B2C integration anticipated later. The system operates a clearance model: invoices in UBL XML are submitted for real-time validation, and only once a unique QR code is returned is the invoice legally valid.

name: Cameroon
keyDate: 2026 Finance Law (Law No. 2025/012 of 17 December 2025) introduces mandatory real-time e-invoicing for all taxable persons and transactions; technical specifications and rollout timeline pending further Ministry of Finance guidance as of this dossier
model: Clearance (Continuous Transaction Control) — mandatory certified e-invoicing solutions, immediate/automatic tax collection mechanisms, and DGI validation/approval of technical platforms
format: TBD — structured electronic format; certified e-invoicing solutions required, specific standard not yet published
summary: Cameroon's 2026 Finance Law (Law No. 2025/012 of 17 December 2025) introduces mandatory real-time e-invoicing for all taxable persons and all transactions — taxable, VAT-exempt, or entirely outside VAT scope — shifting the country from post-filing audits toward Continuous Transaction Controls (CTC). The Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) is developing a central e-invoicing platform, supplemented by accredited third-party providers meeting required standards; an official list of approved providers is to be published. Non-compliant invoices will be denied both VAT-credit and corporate-tax expense deductions, with new financial penalties also applying. The mandate builds on 2024 Finance Law foundations (Article M 8(a)) that already required electronic production tracking and digital accounting systems for targeted sectors (ICT, e-commerce, energy, insurance, beverages, and Large Taxpayers). Foreign companies providing digital services to Cameroon must adapt or face a 3% gross-revenue tax option. Technical specifications and the detailed rollout timeline remain pending as of this dossier.

name: Canada
keyDate: No B2B mandate; B2G electronic submission required
format: UBL 2.1 / Peppol BIS (voluntary); paper, PDF, and structured formats all accepted
summary: Canada has no mandatory e-invoicing regime for B2B transactions at the federal level. Federal suppliers must submit invoices to government electronically through a dedicated portal, but all other e-invoicing remains voluntary. The Canada Revenue Agency administers the Excise Tax Act and publishes guidance on electronic invoicing, while the Peppol network is available for voluntary adoption.

name: Cape Verde
keyDate: Decree Law 79/2020 established compulsory electronic issuance of fiscally relevant documents ("fatura eletrónica"); 2026 Budget Law (Law No. 69/X/2025, published 31 Dec 2025) mandates e-invoicing and updates VAT exemptions, effective 1 January 2026
model: Electronic issuance and communication of fiscal documents to the tax administration, accredited via digital certificate
authority: Direção Nacional das Receitas do Estado (DNRE), Ministério das Finanças
summary: Cape Verde (Cabo Verde) mandates electronic invoicing ("fatura eletrónica") under Decree Law 79/2020, which established compulsory electronic issuance and communication of all fiscally relevant documents, administered by the Direção Nacional das Receitas do Estado (DNRE) within the Ministry of Finance. The 2026 Budget Law (Law No. 69/X/2025, published in the Official Gazette on 31 December 2025) further mandates electronic invoicing and updates VAT exemptions, effective 1 January 2026. DNRE has reported more than half a million e-invoices issued, with the rollout supported by IMF and EU technical partners, and other countries in the region (including Mozambique) have visited Cape Verde to study its implementation.

name: Cayman Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Department for International Tax Cooperation (DITC), Cayman Islands
summary: The Cayman Islands has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme. The territory levies no income tax, corporate tax, VAT, or GST, removing the fiscal basis on which e-invoicing obligations are typically constructed. The DITC focuses exclusively on international tax information exchange frameworks such as CRS, FATCA, Country-by-Country Reporting, and Economic Substance.

name: Central African Republic
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines (DGID)
summary: The Central African Republic has no e-invoicing or transaction-level continuous transaction control mandate in force, announced, or formally proposed. The tax authority, the Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines, completed a broader digital tax modernisation project in 2023 that introduced an eTax platform for online registration, electronic declarations, and payments, but this does not constitute a structured e-invoicing obligation. No legislative instrument, rollout date, or technical format requirement has been identified in the available sources.

name: Chad
keyDate: Mandatory FEN for public expenditure and expanded scope from 1 January 2026
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) / Ministry of Finance, Chad
summary: Chad's 2026 Finance Law, promulgated by President Mahamat Déby and effective 1 January 2026, expanded the mandatory use of the Standardized Electronic Invoice (Facture Électronique Normalisée, FEN) to cover public expenditure processing, public bodies, autonomous local authorities, NGOs, associations, and liberal professions. Suppliers to public contracts must register with the FEN system, and non-compliant invoices are rejected within the public expenditure chain. The technical model and detailed format specification beyond the FEN label are not confirmed in the available sources.

name: Chile
keyDate: Universal since 2018 (pioneer since 2003); B2C boleta electronic invoices gained expanded recipient/payment data requirements from September 2025 (SII Resolution 53/2025)
format: DTE XML, digitally signed, SII CAF-stamped
summary: Chile pioneered e-invoicing in 2003 and has required Documentos Tributarios Electrónicos (DTE) for all taxpayers, universally, since 2018. Invoices are XML, digitally signed, and validated with an SII-issued CAF (Código de Autorización de Folios) stamp before being forwarded to the buyer — there is no SII-provided infrastructure for that forwarding step, unlike some other clearance countries. A December 2024 SII regulation (effective no earlier than September 2025) added expanded recipient and payment information requirements specifically for B2C electronic receipts (boletas).

name: China
keyDate: Nationwide rollout from 1 December 2024
format: Fully digitalised e-fapiao (XML data message, QR code)
summary: China completed the nationwide rollout of the fully digitalised e-fapiao on 1 December 2024, following announcements by the State Taxation Administration on 24 November 2024. The system operates on a clearance model through a nationally unified electronic invoice service platform, replacing earlier paper fapiao and regular e-fapiao formats. Digital invoices carry the same legal validity as paper invoices under the Regulations on the Administration of Invoices of the People's Republic of China.

name: Christmas Island
keyDate: Follows Australia's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Christmas Island does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows Australia's regime directly. Christmas Island's income tax, GST and corporate tax are entirely ATO (Australian Taxation Office) jurisdiction — the local council handles only rates, charges and services, not tax administration. See the Australia dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
keyDate: Follows Australia's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Cocos (Keeling) Islands does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows Australia's regime directly. Cocos (Keeling) Islands shares the same ATO (Australian Taxation Office) tax framework as Christmas Island and mainland Australia. See the Australia dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Colombia
keyDate: Preclearance model since January 2019 (largest taxpayers), compulsory for all taxpayers and all transaction types (B2B/B2C/B2G) since November 2020; extended to equivalent documents (payroll, cash register receipts) and ecommerce platforms by Decree 442 of 29 March 2023
format: UBL 2.1, digitally signed, DIAN-issued CUFE clearance code
authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
summary: Colombia's e-invoicing framework, first introduced in 1995 and progressively updated, moved to a mandatory preclearance model in January 2019 (starting with the largest taxpayers) and became compulsory for all VAT-remitting taxpayers and all transaction types (B2B, B2C, B2G) from November 2020. Every invoice must be cleared by DIAN — which issues a CUFE clearance code — before the supplier can send it to the buyer or ship goods. Decree 442 (29 March 2023) extended the framework to equivalent documents (electronic payroll documents, cash register receipts) and required ecommerce platforms to give vendors the means to issue digital sales invoices.

name: Comoros
keyDate: No evidence of any e-invoicing system, VAT regime, or even a standardised national Tax Identification Number system was found in the sources reviewed
model: Not applicable — no e-invoicing model, VAT system, or standardised taxpayer identification infrastructure was confirmed to exist
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (or equivalent) — exact institutional structure not confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: The Union of the Comoros shows no evidence of an e-invoicing system in the sources reviewed, and the underlying tax administration infrastructure appears considerably less developed than in most other countries covered in this batch. According to IMF-sourced analysis, Comoros does not maintain a formal, standardised, nationwide Tax Identification Number (TIN) system — any taxpayer identifiers that exist are internally assigned, non-standardised, and not publicly verifiable. Formal tax compliance, especially among small businesses, is reported as exceptionally low, with limited taxpayer awareness of registration obligations. Comoros does not operate a formal VAT system, relying instead primarily on indirect and turnover-based taxes. Given the absence of even basic standardised tax administration infrastructure (a working TIN system, a confirmed VAT regime), there is no credible basis for an e-invoicing mandate to exist, and none was found.

name: Cook Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Revenue Management Division (RMD), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Cook Islands
summary: Cook Islands has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or published programme as of August 2026. The Revenue Management Division administers tax and customs under the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, operating an online taxation portal and customs declaration system, but neither authority has announced any e-invoicing requirement or voluntary framework.

name: Costa Rica
keyDate: Comprobantes Electrónicos mandatory economy-wide; version 4.4 mandatory from 1 September 2025 (voluntary from 1 April 2025), replacing v4.3; TRIBU-CR platform launched 6 October 2025
authority: DGT (Dirección General de Tributación), Ministry of Finance
summary: Costa Rica's Comprobantes Electrónicos system, administered by the DGT under the Ministry of Finance, mandates electronic documents in XML format with digital signatures for nearly all taxable transactions. Version 4.4 became mandatory on 1 September 2025 (following voluntary adoption from 1 April 2025), replacing version 4.3, and the entire system is now integrated into the TRIBU-CR (Hacienda Digital) platform launched 6 October 2025, which unifies e-invoicing validation with VAT returns and informative declarations. It is a post-clearance model: DGT validates within 3 hours of submission, rather than before delivery. New elements include the monthly informative return (Form D-270), pre-filled VAT returns, self-billing (Factura Electrónica de Compra) for certain foreign/non-domiciled-supplier purchases, and a new Electronic Payment Receipt (REP) supporting VAT deferral on credit sales.

name: Côte d’Ivoire
keyDate: FNE platform launched 21 July 2025 (registration opened 24 February 2025); originally targeted full completion 1 September 2025, but DGI granted a three-month extension moving final regime-specific deadlines to 1/11/22 December 2025 (RNI/RME/Entreprenant); 52,000+ businesses registered by February 2026
model: Clearance — Facture Normalisée Électronique (FNE) for invoices and Reçu Normalisé Électronique (RNE) for retail receipts, both validated by DGI before delivery to the customer
format: Structured format via DGI's FNE platform, carrying a certification QR code, real-time fiscal number and electronic fiscal seal
summary: Côte d'Ivoire's e-invoicing regime has evolved from the paper/software-based "Facture Normalisée" certified-invoice system (in force since 2005) to a structured Continuous Transaction Control platform, the Facture Normalisée Électronique (FNE), launched by the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) on 21 July 2025. The mandate is rooted in the Annexe fiscale 2025 and implementing Arrêté n°0337 (9 May 2025). Registration opened 24 February 2025, with issuance obligations originally set to complete 1 September 2025; the DGI subsequently granted a three-month extension, moving final regime-specific deadlines to 1 December 2025 (Régime Normal d'Imposition, RNI), 11 December 2025 (Régime des Microentreprises, RME), and 22 December 2025 (Régime de l'Entreprenant). FNE covers B2B, B2C and B2G transactions — one of the broadest scopes in Africa — with a parallel RNE (Reçu Normalisé Électronique) for retail receipts. By February 2026, more than 52,000 businesses were registered, with roughly 80% of large-segment (RNI) taxpayers onboarded. Notable sector exemptions include public utility concessionaires, oil production-sharing entities, airlines, pharmacies, fuel stations, the postal service, banks/insurers, and non-resident companies without a physical presence.

name: Croatia
keyDate: Fiscalization 2.0 mandatory since 1 January 2026
authority: Porezna uprava (Tax Administration), Ministry of Finance
summary: Croatia's "Fiscalization 2.0" reform, effective 1 January 2026, mandates structured e-invoicing (eRačun) for B2B and B2G transactions between VAT-registered businesses, in a Croatia-specific CIUS (HR-FISK 2.0) built on EN 16931. B2C sales require real-time fiscalization reporting to the Tax Administration regardless of payment method, though a traditional receipt (not necessarily a structured e-invoice) is acceptable for the consumer as long as the transaction data is reported. The goal is that essentially every taxable transaction is digitally captured, with very few exceptions.

name: Cuba
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Oficina Nacional de Administración Tributaria (ONAT), Cuba
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Cuba in the sources reviewed. No ONAT-specific mandate, law, or proposal was found; sources are generic directory/vendor content.

name: Curaçao
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Curaçao is an autonomous constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands with its own independent tax administration, the Belastingdienst Curaçao. No e-invoicing mandate, formal programme, or announced legislative instrument has been identified in any available official source. The tax authority operates an online filing portal for wage tax and other declarations, but this is unrelated to any e-invoicing obligation.

name: Cyprus
keyDate: B2G reception mandatory since April 2019; no B2B or B2C mandate
authority: Ministry of Finance / Treasury of the Republic
summary: Cyprus has implemented the EU Directive 2014/55/EU requirement for public sector bodies to receive and process structured e-invoices compliant with EN 16931, effective April 2019 for central bodies and April 2020 for sub-central bodies. Supplier issuance remains voluntary and the exchange network is Peppol. There is no B2B or B2C mandate and no real-time VAT reporting obligation.

name: Czechia
keyDate: B2G e-invoice acceptance mandatory since 1 October 2016 (Act No. 134/2016 Sb.); Kontrolní hlášení (VAT Control Statement) e-reporting live since 1 January 2016; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, no domestic mandate announced; EU ViDA intra-EU DRR applies from 1 July 2030, national implementation not expected before 2029
model: Post-audit (no CTC/clearance) — invoices exchanged directly between parties; Financial Administration controls ex-post via Kontrolní hlášení cross-matching
format: ISDOC (national UBL 2.0-customised XML, voluntary) for B2B; EN 16931 (UBL 2.1, ISDOC, or EDIFACT syntax) mandatory for B2G acceptance; Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 usable but uncommon
summary: The Czech Republic explicitly operates a post-audit, non-CTC VAT system: the tax authority does not pre-validate or clear invoices, which are exchanged directly between parties. Public contracting authorities have been required to accept EN 16931-compliant e-invoices since 1 October 2016 (Act No. 134/2016 Sb., transposing EU Directive 2014/55/EU), but suppliers have no issuance obligation. Domestically, B2B e-invoicing remains entirely voluntary — Czechia's own national XML format, ISDOC (a UBL 2.0 customisation launched 2008), is built into most Czech ERP/accounting systems, making voluntary structured e-invoicing widespread in practice despite no legal mandate. The core digital-VAT compliance tool is the Kontrolní hlášení (VAT Control Statement), a mandatory transaction-level e-reporting filing live since 1 January 2016, used for ex-post cross-matching of supplier/customer entries to combat carousel/missing-trader fraud — this carries real penalty exposure (CZK 1,000-50,000 fixed fines, up to CZK 500,000 discretionary). Czechia is positioned as an 'aligned follower' on EU ViDA: mandatory intra-EU digital reporting requirements (DRR) apply from 1 July 2030, but no domestic B2B e-invoicing mandate has been announced, with national implementation not expected before 2029. The short-lived real-time sales-reporting system EET was abolished 1 January 2023; a draft 'EET 2.0' law is reported, targeted for 2027, but not enacted.

name: Denmark
keyDate: Digital bookkeeping live
summary: B2G e-invoicing is long mandatory and the Bookkeeping Act requires digital systems capable of e-invoice exchange — a de facto soft mandate without a formal B2B one.

name: Djibouti
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Djibouti in the sources reviewed. No government-confirmed mandate, law, or proposal was found; sources are generic vendor content targeting field-sales distributors.

name: Dominica
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Dominica in the sources reviewed. name: Dominican Republic
keyDate: Law 32-23 and Decree 587-24 effective 10 October 2024 (DGII Notice 20-24); phased rollout from large national corporations (since May 2023) through medium businesses to small enterprises, closing with smaller taxpayer waves through May 2026; contingency mechanism (Instructivo de Contingencia de FE) published February 2026
model: Post-clearance — electronic invoices (e-CF) sent simultaneously to DGII and the buyer, digitally signed and validated in real time
format: Local XML — electronic tax receipts (e-CF, Comprobante Fiscal Electrónico)
summary: The Dominican Republic's e-invoicing regime is governed by Law 32-23 on Electronic Invoicing and its regulating Decree 587-24, detailed in DGII Notice 20-24, effective from 10 October 2024. The model is a post-clearance system: electronic tax receipts (e-CF), in a locally-defined XML format, must be digitally signed and sent simultaneously to both the DGII (for real-time validation) and the buyer. Rollout has proceeded in phased waves since May 2023, starting with large national corporations, then medium-sized businesses, and closing with small enterprises through May 2026. The law and decree apply to all individuals and entities in the country engaging in transactions involving goods or services, whether paid or free. The DGII provides a free online invoicing tool so SMEs and freelancers can issue compliant e-CFs without needing their own billing software, and published a formal contingency mechanism (Instructivo de Contingencia de FE) in February 2026 to handle technical or connectivity outages.

name: DR Congo
keyDate: Pilot began September 2024 (DGI); mandatory rollout began 1 December 2025; grace period ended with a compliance deadline of 15 May 2026; support programme distributing 4,000 free electronic fiscal devices launched 1 March 2026
model: Standardized invoicing ("facture normalisée") via secure electronic fiscal devices (EFDs) directly connected to the tax authority
format: Not confirmed in sources reviewed; issued via certified EFD (Invoicing Unit / Invoicing Control Module architecture)
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI); Ministry of Finance
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) is rolling out a standardized electronic invoicing system ("facture normalisée"), led by the Directorate General of Taxes (DGI) and the Ministry of Finance. A pilot began in September 2024, with mandatory rollout starting 1 December 2025 following early implementation difficulties; a transitional grace period followed, ending with a formal compliance deadline of 15 May 2026, after which full enforcement applies. To support adoption, the Ministry of Finance launched a programme on 1 March 2026 distributing 4,000 electronic fiscal devices (EFDs) free of charge to eligible VAT-registered businesses without an EFD exemption, on a first-come, first-served basis.

name: Ecuador
keyDate: Universal for General regime and RIMPE Entrepreneur taxpayers; RIMPE Popular Business taxpayers (income up to USD 20,000) not required, may use a simplified sales note
format: XML, with optional PDF RIDE (Representación Impresa del Documento Electrónico) on buyer request
summary: Ecuador mandates electronic invoicing clearance for all tax-registered companies in the General regime, submitted as XML to the SRI for validation before delivery to the buyer. Within the RIMPE simplified regime, the distinction matters: RIMPE Entrepreneur taxpayers (annual income USD 20,001-300,000) must invoice electronically, while RIMPE Popular Business taxpayers (income up to USD 20,000) are not required to and may use a simplified sales note instead. A valid electronic signature is a prerequisite for issuing any electronic receipt.

name: Egypt
keyDate: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses from 2023; B2C e-receipts rolling through 2025
summary: Egypt operates a fully mandatory clearance-based e-invoicing system supervised by the Egyptian Tax Authority. All VAT-registered businesses must issue JSON or XML invoices cleared in real time through the ETA portal, with paper invoices no longer valid for input VAT recovery or cost deduction as of 2023. B2C electronic receipts continue to roll out in phased waves, with the most recent wave taking effect 15 September 2025 under ETA Resolution No. 281 of 2025.

name: El Salvador
keyDate: Decree 487/2022 approved 30 August 2022, making DTE mandatory; Ministry of Finance estimated ~18 months for all sectors to be required to implement; DTE Compliance Regulation v1.1 (June 2024) governs current technical requirements; full rollout completed across taxpayer groups 2024-2025
model: Clearance — DTEs validated by the Tax Authority (Reception Seal), either via prior transmission (cleared before delivery to customer) or deferred transmission (delivered to customer, validated afterward)
format: JSON, digitally signed per the JWS (JSON Web Signature) standard
summary: El Salvador's e-invoicing mandate originates from Decree 487/2022, approved by the Asamblea Legislativa on 30 August 2022, reforming the tax code to make Documento Tributario Electrónico (DTE) mandatory — explicitly inspired by e-invoicing regimes already in place in Colombia, Argentina, Peru, and Mexico. The Ministry of Finance estimated approximately 18 months for all sectors to be brought into the mandate following the decree. Current technical requirements are governed by the DTE Compliance Regulation (version 1.1, June 2024), which defines ten distinct DTE document types (electronic invoice, tax credit voucher, export invoice, excluded-subject invoice, delivery note, credit note, debit note, settlement voucher, donation voucher, and accounting settlement document). Companies may use either prior transmission (document sent to the Tax Authority first, must obtain the Reception Seal before delivery to the customer) or deferred transmission (signed document delivered to the customer first, then sent for validation). Electronic signatures must comply with the JWS (JSON Web Signature) standard, and a graphical representation (PDF or similar) must accompany every DTE.

authority: Dirección General de Impuestos, Equatorial Guinea
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Equatorial Guinea in the sources reviewed.
