name: Estonia
keyDate: Mandatory B2B from 2027 (planned)
format: EN 16931 (UBL 2.1 / UN/CEFACT CII); local eXML 1.2 permitted
authority: Ministry of Finance / MTA (Estonian Tax and Customs Board)
summary: Estonia has mandated B2G e-invoicing since 2019 and, from 1 July 2025, any buyer registered as an e-invoice recipient in the commercial register may require structured e-invoices from suppliers under an amended Accounting Act. A full B2B mandate is planned for 2027, accompanied by abolition of the EUR 1,000 VAT-reporting threshold, pending final legislation.

name: Eswatini
keyDate: VAT E-Invoicing Regulations No. 25 of 2026 published, establishing legal basis for Electronic Fiscal Documents (EFDs); technical rules issued under Legal Notice No. 111 of 2026, in force from 15 July 2026, with phased sector rollout starting with wholesale and retail
model: Clearance-adjacent — each transaction processed through an accredited Electronic Fiscal Device (EFD), assigned a unique identifier, and transmitted to the ERS e-invoicing system in real time or within 15 days if connectivity is unavailable
format: Structured fiscal data via accredited EFDs (POS or approved system integration); specific XML/data schema not detailed in sources reviewed
summary: Eswatini has enacted a legally mandatory e-invoicing and fiscalisation regime, the VAT (Electronic Submission of Fiscal Data and Return-Supporting Records) Notice 2026, issued under Legal Notice No. 111 of 2026 and in force since 15 July 2026, alongside VAT E-Invoicing Regulations No. 25 of 2026 which establish Electronic Fiscal Documents (EFDs) as the legal mechanism. The reform combines B2B e-invoicing, POS fiscal device integration, and real-time invoice reporting to ERS, aimed at closing an estimated E4 billion annual VAT compliance gap without raising VAT rates. Rollout is explicitly phased by sector, with the wholesale and retail sectors identified as the strategic starting point given their high transaction volumes; ERS began structured stakeholder engagement with that sector in July 2026. Because the law is in force but the rollout is sector-by-sector rather than universal, this is classified as 'phasing' rather than fully 'live'.

name: Ethiopia
keyDate: Electronic invoicing has been in place since the 2018 Tax Invoice Utilization and Administration Directive No. 149/2018; substantially overhauled by the Electronic Invoice System Administration Directive No. 1142/2026 (issued ~July 2026), a freestanding 31-article clearance-based regime replacing the prior 2-article framework
model: Clearance — every invoice must receive an Invoice Reference Number (IRN), Receipt Reference Number (RRN), and QR code from the Ministry of Revenues' central system before it is legally valid
format: Structured electronic invoice per Ministry of Revenues technical specifications; a sample invoice template is annexed to Directive No. 1142/2026
summary: Ethiopia has operated a clearance-based e-invoicing regime since the Tax Invoice Utilization and Administration Directive No. 149/2018, but the Ministry of Revenues substantially overhauled the framework with the Electronic Invoice System Administration Directive No. 1142/2026 (issued around July 2026), replacing the prior two-article regime with a freestanding, 31-article directive and two technical annexes. Every invoice must now receive an Invoice Reference Number (IRN), Receipt Reference Number (RRN), and QR code from the Ministry's central system before it is legally valid. The new directive introduces multi-track accreditation (separate tracks for system suppliers, SaaS providers, marketplace operators, and exclusive-use developers), mandatory offline resilience for 26 listed business sectors, an Authority-run Cloud Sales Registration System, and manual QR invoices as a last resort, all overseen by a newly established Inspection and Accreditation Board.

name: Falkland Islands
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The Falkland Islands operates its own independent tax administration under the Falkland Islands Government Taxation Office, covering income tax, corporation tax, and related obligations. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, voluntary framework, or published programme has been identified in any official source. The territory remains outside the scope of any e-invoicing requirement as of August 2026.

name: Faroe Islands
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The Faroe Islands is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, outside the EU and Danish VAT area, with its own independent tax authority, TAKS. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or formal programme has been identified in any of the available sources. The territory operates a highly automated direct-tax withholding system, but this is distinct from any structured e-invoicing obligation.

name: Fiji
keyDate: VAT Monitoring System (VMS) fiscalisation live since 2017-2018; Phase 3 participants transitioning from VMS v2 to v3, with reaccreditation required by end of 2026
model: Fiscal devices (VMS) — signed receipts issued at point of sale, data transmitted in real time to FRCS via Virtual (V-SDC) or External (E-SDC) Sales Data Controller
summary: Fiji operates the VAT Monitoring System (VMS), a fiscalisation-based e-invoicing regime administered by the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS), live since as early as 2017-2018 — among the earliest such systems in the Pacific region. VMS unifies B2C, B2B and B2G transactions: every receipt or invoice is digitally signed and simultaneously transmitted to FRCS, either online via a Virtual Sales Data Controller (V-SDC) or offline via an External Sales Data Controller (E-SDC) with delayed sync, a design suited to a region prone to natural disasters. FRCS, which collects over 85% of government revenue, built the system with Data Tech International (DTI) using the TaxCore platform. All accredited vendors are currently transitioning from VMS version 2 to version 3, with Phase 3 participants required to reaccredit by the end of 2026. Fiji's model has since been adopted regionally, with Samoa (TIMS), Vanuatu (VSMS) and Papua New Guinea (GMS) following the same fiscalisation approach.

name: Finland
keyDate: B2G mandatory since April 2021; B2B buyer right since 2020; EU ViDA cross-border mandate from 1 July 2030
format: Finvoice 3.0 / TEAPPSXML 3.0 / Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 (EN 16931 compliant)
summary: Finland enforces mandatory e-invoicing for B2G transactions as of April 2021, under the e-Invoicing Act 241/2019 implementing EU Directive 2014/55/EU. Business buyers with annual turnover above EUR 10,000 may demand structured e-invoices from their suppliers, but there is no general B2B issuance mandate. The EU ViDA reform is expected to introduce mandatory cross-border B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting from 1 July 2030.

name: France
keyDate: Mandatory B2B receiving obligation from 1 Sep 2026; issuing for large/ETI from 1 Sep 2026, SMEs/micro from 1 Sep 2027
model: 5-corner CTC via certified Plateformes Agréées (PAs) + PPF + e-reporting
format: EN 16931 compliant: UBL 2.1, UN/CEFACT CII, Factur-X (hybrid PDF/XML)
summary: France is rolling out mandatory B2B e-invoicing in two phases under a Continuous Transaction Controls model. From 1 September 2026, all French VAT-registered businesses must be able to receive e-invoices, and large and intermediate-sized enterprises must also issue them; SMEs and micro-enterprises follow from 1 September 2027. All invoices must flow through government-certified Plateformes Agréées (formerly PDPs), which simultaneously transmit data to the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF) and hence to the DGFiP.

name: French Guiana
keyDate: Receive by 1 Sep 2026; issue (large/ETI) 1 Sep 2026, issue (SME/micro) 1 Sep 2027
format: Structured electronic invoice via accredited platform (specific format names not confirmed in sources)
summary: French Guiana is a full French département and région d'outre-mer (DROM), fiscally and constitutionally integrated into France. France's national e-invoicing and e-reporting reform therefore applies directly, with all businesses subject to French VAT required to receive electronic invoices by 1 September 2026 and to issue them on a phased schedule extending to 1 September 2027. The reform uses a decentralised 5-corner (Y-model) architecture built around state-accredited platforms (PAs) and the Public Invoice Portal (PPF).

name: French Polynesia
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Direction des Impôts et des Contributions Publiques, French Polynesia
summary: French Polynesia operates its own independent tax administration, distinct from any parent/host state, but no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been found. French Overseas Collectivity (COM) with its own autonomous tax regime (including its own VAT) — explicitly outside the scope of France's 2026 e-invoicing/e-reporting reform, per that reform's own COM exemption. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Gabon
keyDate: 2026 Finance Law (Loi n°041/2025) makes e-invoicing effective 1 January 2026 for VAT/tax deductibility purposes, with full mandatory enforcement from 1 July 2026 (a 6-month transition period during which customs duty documentation could still substitute)
model: Clearance — standardized electronic invoices (FEN) issued through DGI-approved systems, transmitted to the tax authority for real-time validation and a unique QR code before being legally valid
format: FEN — Facture Électronique Normalisée (standardized electronic invoice); free government e-DEF portal or certified private solutions
summary: Gabon's E-Fact system, established by the 2026 Finance Law (Loi n°041/2025), mandates a standardized electronic invoice (Facture Électronique Normalisée, FEN) for virtually every business transaction — B2B, B2C, B2G, and cross-border — conducted by any person liable to corporate tax, business profits tax, the simplified flat tax, or VAT. The mandate became effective 1 January 2026 for VAT and income-tax deductibility purposes (the FEN, bearing a QR code, is now the only valid invoice format for claiming VAT credits or expense deductions in B2B), with a 6-month transition period during which customs duty documentation could still substitute, ending with full mandatory enforcement from 1 July 2026. Invoices are issued through DGI-approved systems — either the free government e-DEF portal or certified private solutions — and validated in real time with a unique QR code, with invoice issuance itself serving as the e-reporting mechanism. Penalties are severe: fines of up to 100% of the transaction value for failing to issue a compliant e-invoice, with potential business closure for severe infractions.

name: Gambia
keyDate: Mandatory e-invoicing for VAT proposed in the 2026 Budget Speech (presented to the National Assembly 5 December 2025); Appropriation Act 2026 approved, moving the mandate into an implementation-planning phase; draft Electronic Invoicing Regulations 2025 submitted for stakeholder validation from July 2025 — no live technical requirement or confirmed implementation date yet
model: Not yet confirmed — draft regulations propose a centralized system for receiving electronic invoices
format: Not yet confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: The Gambia has approved, via its 2026 national budget, the introduction of mandatory electronic invoicing for VAT-registered taxpayers, with potential extension to other taxes. The Gambia Revenue Authority (GRA) publicly presented the e-invoicing project on 8 July 2025 and has since worked on draft Electronic Invoicing Regulations 2025, submitted for validation with taxpayer and business stakeholder input. The National Assembly approved the Appropriation Act 2026 (formally passed 9 December 2025), moving the legal mandate for this digital tax transformation into an implementation-planning phase — but as of the sources reviewed, the regulatory framework remains under development, with no confirmed technical requirements, format, platform, or firm implementation timeline published. This is a genuine government-adopted policy commitment (not merely a proposal from an individual official), but it has not yet become an enforceable, technically-specified mandate.

name: Georgia
keyDate: RS.ge universal
summary: Tax invoices are issued electronically through the RS.ge portal — effectively universal e-invoicing for VAT payers.

name: Germany
keyDate: Receive: live Jan 2025; Issue: Jan 2027 (>€800k turnover), Jan 2028 (all)
format: XRechnung (XML) / ZUGFeRD 2.0.1+ (hybrid PDF+XML) / Peppol BIS 3.0; all EN 16931 compliant
summary: Since 1 January 2025 every German-established business must be able to receive structured EN 16931 e-invoices for domestic B2B transactions, with no grace period on the reception side. Mandatory issuance follows a phased timeline: from 1 January 2027 for businesses whose prior-year turnover exceeded €800,000, and from 1 January 2028 for all remaining businesses. Germany operates a decentralised model with no central government clearance platform for B2B invoices; exchange occurs directly between trading parties.

name: Ghana
keyDate: Phased onboarding via GRA's Electronic VAT Invoicing System since 2022; Phase Two added ~2,000 taxpayers from September 2024; broader mandate (including non-resident digital platforms, no revenue threshold) reported effective from January 2026
model: Clearance — invoices approved by GRA's Virtual Sales Data Controller (VSDC) before issuance to customers
format: TBC — transmitted via GRA's E-VAT/VSDC system; specific schema not confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: The Ghana Revenue Authority operates a phased Electronic VAT Invoicing System (E-VAT), onboarding VAT-registered taxpayers in waves — Phase Two added roughly 2,000 additional taxpayers from September 2024. Under this system, invoices are cleared in real time through GRA's Virtual Sales Data Controller (VSDC) before being issued to customers. Industry reporting describes a broader E-VAT mandate reportedly effective from January 2026 covering all VAT-registered businesses, including non-resident digital platforms, with no revenue threshold, and extending to tax invoices, sales receipts, refunds, credit/debit notes, purchase records, and hospitality statements of account.

name: Gibraltar
keyDate: No mandate
authority: HM Government of Gibraltar, Income Tax Office
summary: Gibraltar has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme. The Income Tax Office administers income tax and corporation tax under the Income Tax Act 2010, and has moved to electronic submission of tax returns, but this is distinct from any e-invoicing obligation. Gibraltar has no VAT and is treated as a third country for EU VAT purposes, removing the EU Directive 2014/55/EU framework that drives mandates elsewhere in Europe.

name: Greece
keyDate: B2B Phase A live Mar 2026; Phase B from Oct 2026
summary: Greece enacted Law 5222/2025 in July 2025, establishing mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing via the myDATA clearance platform. Phase A, covering large enterprises with 2023 revenues above EUR 1 million, became mandatory on 2 March 2026 following a one-month postponement, with enforcement from 3 May 2026. Phase B, covering all remaining VAT-registered businesses, begins 1 October 2026 with a transition period to 31 December 2026.

name: Greenland
keyDate: Mandatory B2G digital invoicing from 1 March 2025
authority: Government of Greenland (Naalakkersuisut) / Danish Business Authority (NemHandelsRegister)
summary: Greenland mandates digital invoicing for all suppliers of goods and services to public authorities, effective 1 March 2025, under an executive order published 11 November 2024. Invoices must be in OIOUBL format and exchanged through the NemHandel platform; non-compliant invoices are rejected and reset the payment clock. Business-to-business e-invoicing remains voluntary, and smaller entities may qualify for an exemption based on an annual turnover threshold of DKK 300,000.

name: Grenada
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Grenada in the sources reviewed. GTAX, launched 2024 with World Bank funding, is a general digital tax administration system (online filing/payment for VAT, PAYE, CIT) — not a structured e-invoicing mandate. No evidence of e-invoicing specifically was found.

name: Guadeloupe
keyDate: Follows France's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Guadeloupe does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows France's regime directly. Guadeloupe is a full French département/région (DROM), fiscally integrated into France. French tax law, including the national e-invoicing/e-reporting reform, applies directly. See the France dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Guam
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation
summary: Guam operates its own independent tax administration, the Department of Revenue and Taxation, which administers a mirrored version of the US Internal Revenue Code as local law. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been identified in any available official source. The territory's online payment and filing infrastructure covers tax payments and GRT returns but does not constitute or announce an e-invoicing obligation.

name: Guatemala
keyDate: FEL exclusive system for tax documents since 1 July 2023 (SAT Board Agreement No. 13-2018); gradual mandatory rollout by sector since 2019
format: XML, SAT XSD schema, electronic signature required
summary: Guatemala's Factura Electrónica en Línea (FEL) system, which replaced the earlier FACE regime, became the exclusive system for issuing tax documents from 1 July 2023 under SAT Board Agreement No. 13-2018, following a gradual sector-by-sector mandatory rollout since 2019. Documents must be XML, digitally signed, and validated by an SAT-certified Certifier before delivery to the customer, receiving a unique certification code and UUID. A Provisional Invoice Complement (FACP), effective from 31 May 2024, supports exporters (particularly of perishable goods) who need to ship before definitive export documentation is ready.

name: Guernsey
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Guernsey has no e-invoicing mandate, no announced e-invoicing programme, and no structured e-invoicing format or model in place. The Revenue Service administers income tax and social security contributions but does not operate a VAT or GST system, removing the primary driver behind most e-invoicing mandates globally. The island's 2025 Budget proposal to introduce GST from 2027 is worth monitoring, but nothing in the available sources confirms any e-invoicing obligation or programme linked to that proposal.

name: Guinea
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Guinea in the sources reviewed. No DGI-specific mandate, law, or proposal was found; both sources are generic directory/vendor content.

name: Guinea-Bissau
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Direção Geral das Contribuições e Impostos (DGCI), Guinea-Bissau
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Guinea-Bissau in the sources reviewed. No DGCI-specific mandate, law, or proposal was found; both sources are generic directory/vendor content.

name: Guyana
keyDate: No confirmed e-invoicing mandate, platform, or legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed; standard paper/manual tax invoice requirements under the VAT Act, No. 10 of 2005 remain in force
model: Not confirmed in sources reviewed — no e-invoicing model identified; standard VAT tax invoices and sales invoices are manually issued per statutory content rules
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Guyana in the sources reviewed, despite the country's prior 'proposed' classification. The Guyana Revenue Authority (GRA), Guyana's tax administration, publishes standard VAT invoice content requirements under the VAT Act, No. 10 of 2005 (Chapter 81:05) — every VAT-registered business must issue a Tax Invoice with prescribed fields (registration number, description, tax amount, serial number, date), or, for small cash sales under G$10,000, a simplified Sales Invoice — but these are manual/paper-oriented statutory requirements, not a structured electronic invoicing or Continuous Transaction Control system. GRA's digitisation efforts to date (ASYCUDA World for customs since 2018, Optimal Revenue Management System eServices since February 2021, online banking payment integrations since 2015) focus on payments, customs, and return filing rather than invoice-level e-invoicing.

name: Haiti
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Haiti in the sources reviewed. The only other banked source (Taxilla's UAE e-invoicing guide) is unrelated to Haiti and was excluded. No evidence of a mandate, platform, or proposal was found.

name: Honduras
keyDate: SAR (Servicio de Administración de Rentas) operates a Billing Regime Regulation offering authorized electronic invoicing alongside the traditional CAI (Código de Autorización de Impresión) printed-invoice system; implementation is proceeding in phases by economic sector, taxpayer size, and invoicing volume, but no universal mandate is yet complete
model: Authorization-based — businesses formally request SAR authorization to issue electronic fiscal documents; CAI (authorized-printing) remains the base/default system alongside it
summary: Honduras's invoicing regime is governed by SAR's Billing Regime Regulation (Régimen de Facturación), which establishes permitted billing modalities, mandatory invoice fields, and penalties for non-compliance. The traditional base system is CAI (Código de Autorización de Impresión — Printing Authorization Code), under which businesses obtain SAR authorization to print invoices; electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) is also available under specific SAR authorization, and SAR is progressively defining mandatory phases by economic sector, taxpayer size, and invoicing volume. Honduras trails several Central American peers with completed mandatory e-invoicing (Guatemala's FEL since 2022, Costa Rica since 2018, Panama's SFEP, El Salvador's DTE since 2022) — Honduras has not yet completed a universal mandate, making 'voluntary/authorization-based, phasing in progress' the most accurate characterization.

name: Hong Kong
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Hong Kong in the sources reviewed. All sources are third-party vendor guides describing general e-invoicing readiness advice; none cite a specific IRD law, regulation, or mandate — consistent with Hong Kong having no e-invoicing mandate as of the sources reviewed.

name: Hungary
keyDate: RTIR since 2018/2021; electricity/gas B2B e-invoicing mandate since 1 Jul 2025; broader receipt data-reporting from 1 Sep 2026; full structured e-invoicing mandate proposed under ViDA (not yet final legislation)
model: Real-time invoice reporting (RTIR/CTC), moving toward full structured e-invoicing under a proposed ViDA-aligned model
format: NAV Online Számla XML (reporting); any legally valid electronic format (PDF, XML, EDI) accepted for the invoice itself today
summary: Hungary's core obligation today is Real-Time Invoice Reporting (RTIR): invoice data for in-scope transactions must be reported to NAV via the Online Invoice System, but the invoice itself can still be paper, PDF, or structured XML — Hungary does not yet require a specific structured e-invoice format for all domestic B2B/B2C invoices. Two additions have layered on: a sector-specific mandatory e-invoicing requirement for electricity/gas supply to non-private customers since 1 July 2025, and a broader receipt data-reporting obligation from 1 September 2026. Separately, NAV has published a conceptual (not yet legislated) framework describing a move to a full ViDA-aligned structured e-invoicing model, in which XML would become the sole legally valid invoice for domestic B2B, cross-border EU B2B, and B2G.

name: Iceland
keyDate: B2G mandatory from 1 January 2020
authority: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs; Fjársýsla ríkisins (Financial Management Authority) as Peppol Authority
summary: Iceland has had a mandatory B2G e-invoicing regime since 1 January 2020, requiring all suppliers to public authorities to issue structured electronic invoices compliant with EN 16931 via the Peppol network using Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 or UBL 2.1 under the national CIUS TS-236. The obligation was transposed from EU Directive 2014/55/EU via Regulation 44/2019. There is no B2B or B2C e-invoicing mandate; voluntary adoption in the private sector is growing but remains market-driven.

name: India
keyDate: Mandatory B2B/B2G above ₹5 crore from 1 August 2023; B2C pilot voluntary from September 2024
summary: India operates a centralised, real-time clearance-based e-invoicing system under the GST framework, mandatory for B2B, B2G and export transactions for taxpayers with aggregate annual turnover above ₹5 crore as of 1 August 2023. Suppliers must submit invoices in a prescribed JSON format to an authorised Invoice Registration Portal before issuance; the IRP validates, digitally signs, assigns an Invoice Reference Number and returns a QR code that must appear on the final invoice. A voluntary B2C pilot was recommended by the GST Council in September 2024 and is in progress.

name: Indonesia
keyDate: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses since 2016; Coretax platform live from 2026
summary: Indonesia mandates clearance-based e-invoicing for all VAT-registered businesses via the e-Faktur system, now migrating to the Coretax platform. Every VAT invoice must be submitted to the Directorate General of Taxes for real-time validation and approval before it is legally valid. Invoices not issued and cleared through the official system are considered invalid for VAT purposes.

name: Iran
keyDate: Moadian system live, phased rollout ongoing
summary: Iran operates a clearance-based e-invoicing regime under the Store Terminals and Taxpayers System law, requiring invoices to be issued through the Moadian tax platform. The Iranian National Tax Administration (INTA) administers the system. Academic research published in INTA's own journal confirms the system is live and identifies ongoing implementation challenges.

name: Iraq
keyDate: No domestic e-invoicing mandate or regulation exists as of the sources reviewed; a narrow, customs-specific electronic verification requirement for certificates of origin and commercial invoices (via ASYCUDA) becomes mandatory for customs clearance from 10 July 2026
model: Not applicable domestically — no clearance/post-audit model exists; various formats (paper, PDF, structured electronic, portal key-in) are all accepted
format: No specific format required — paper, PDF, structured electronic, and portal key-in invoices all accepted for domestic purposes
authority: General Commission for Taxes (GCT); General Customs Authority (for the separate customs verification requirement)
summary: Iraq has no domestic e-invoicing mandate or regulation as of the sources reviewed — electronic invoicing is legal and may be used voluntarily, but no businesses are currently required to comply with any specific format or platform, and Iraq does not levy a general VAT (only a category-specific service sales tax and corporate income tax). The General Commission for Taxes (GCT) has no formal e-invoicing system in place, though a future initiative connecting taxpayer systems for real-time submission has been discussed speculatively by industry vendors, with no confirmed timeline. Separately and more concretely, Iraq's General Customs Authority has mandated electronic verification of certificates of origin and commercial invoices via the ASYCUDA customs platform for trade documentation, becoming fully mandatory at all Iraqi border points from 10 July 2026 — but this is a customs-clearance verification requirement, not a general domestic business-to-business e-invoicing mandate.

name: Ireland
keyDate: Phase One (large corporates, domestic B2B) 1 November 2028; Phase Two (cross-border EU B2B zero-rate) November 2029; Phase Three (full EU ViDA cross-border) 1 July 2030
model: Structured e-invoicing with real-time data reporting to Revenue (VAT Modernisation programme, aligned with EU ViDA)
format: EN 16931 structured electronic format (e.g. XML) — PDFs and scanned paper documents explicitly excluded
summary: Ireland's Revenue has confirmed a three-phase 'VAT Modernisation' rollout aligned with the EU's VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative. From 1 November 2028 (Phase One), VAT-registered 'large corporates' (those managed by Revenue's Large Corporates Division, established or with a fixed establishment in Ireland) must issue EN 16931-compliant structured e-invoices for domestic B2B transactions and report a subset of invoice data to Revenue in real time; all businesses in Ireland must be able to receive structured e-invoices from that date. Phase Two (November 2029) extends the requirement to VAT-registered businesses involved in cross-border EU B2B trade under zero-rate VAT. Phase Three (1 July 2030) applies full EU ViDA rules to all cross-border EU B2B transactions. Revenue published its implementation plan in October 2025 and confirmed the Phase One large-corporate scope on 10 February 2026.

name: Isle of Man
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Isle of Man Treasury, Income Tax Division
summary: Isle of Man operates its own independent tax administration, distinct from any parent/host state, but no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been found. Crown Dependency with its own Treasury and Income Tax Division; shares a VAT/customs union with the UK under the Common Purse Agreement (unlike Jersey/Guernsey, which are outside the UK VAT area). No e-invoicing mandate found. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Italy
keyDate: Mandatory B2B/B2C from 1 Jan 2019; full coverage (all taxpayer sizes) from 1 Jan 2024
format: FatturaPA XML (national standard, aligned with EN 16931)
summary: Italy is Europe's pioneer in mandatory e-invoicing, having required all domestic B2B, B2C and B2G invoices to transit the government's Sistema di Interscambio (SdI) platform in FatturaPA XML format since 2019, with full coverage of all taxpayer sizes achieved on 1 January 2024. The SdI operates as an active clearance hub, validating every invoice against more than 100 formal controls before routing it to the recipient. Italy's authorisation to maintain this domestic mandate runs to 31 December 2027 under EU Council derogation, bridging the period until the ViDA cross-border framework takes effect.

name: Jamaica
keyDate: An electronic invoicing system for Tax Administration Jamaica (TAJ) was proposed by the Opposition Spokesperson on Finance during the 2026/27 Budget Debate in the House of Representatives on 12 March 2026 — this is a political/legislative proposal, not a government-adopted initiative, and no government commitment, timeline, or enabling legislation had been confirmed as of the sources reviewed
model: Proposed only — envisioned as a system automatically transmitting sales transaction data to TAJ at the moment of sale, replacing the current model where businesses upload transaction records after the fact
format: Not specified — this remains a policy proposal, not an implemented or legislated system
authority: Tax Administration Jamaica (TAJ) — the proposal's implementing authority if adopted
summary: Jamaica has no government-adopted e-invoicing mandate. The concrete development identified is a proposal — not a government commitment — made by Opposition Spokesperson on Finance Julian Robinson during the House of Representatives' 2026/27 Budget Debate on 12 March 2026, recommending that Tax Administration Jamaica (TAJ) implement an electronic invoicing system. Robinson argued the current model, where businesses are responsible for uploading transaction records to TAJ after sales occur, creates a reporting gap due to incomplete submissions and administrative delays; he estimated an e-invoicing system automatically transmitting sales data at the point of sale could generate approximately J$8.6 billion in additional annual tax revenue without raising tax rates, citing case studies from Mexico, Uruguay, Peru, and Chile. As of the sources reviewed, this remains an opposition budget-debate proposal, not an adopted government policy — no TAJ commitment, enabling legislation, technical specification, or implementation timeline has been confirmed.

name: Japan
keyDate: Qualified Invoice System effective 1 October 2023; e-invoicing via JP PINT/Peppol promoted but not mandated
format: JP PINT (Japan's localisation of Peppol BIS Billing 3.0)
summary: Japan's Qualified Invoice System (QIS), effective 1 October 2023, requires NTA-registered suppliers to issue qualified invoices with specific tax detail for buyers to claim input tax credit; paper invoices remain legal. Structured e-invoicing via JP PINT, Japan's Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 customisation, is promoted by the Digital Agency (Japan's Peppol Authority since September 2021) but is not legally mandated. The Electronic Book Preservation Act separately requires searchable, tamper-proof digital storage of trading documents, including invoices, for 10 years.

name: Jersey
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Jersey, a Crown Dependency with its own independent tax administration, has no e-invoicing mandate, clearance platform, or announced programme. Revenue Jersey administers Goods and Services Tax under the Goods and Services Tax (Jersey) Law 2007 and requires GST-registered businesses to issue invoices containing specified fields, but paper and electronic invoices are equally valid provided those fields are present. No pre-approval, real-time transmission, or structured digital format is required.

name: Jordan
keyDate: Mandatory nationwide (B2B, B2C, B2G) from 1 April 2025 (Phase 2)
format: XML or JSON, digitally signed and encrypted
authority: ISTD (Income and Sales Tax Department), with the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship
summary: Jordan's JoFotara national e-invoicing platform became mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers on 1 April 2025 (Phase 2), covering B2B, B2C and B2G transactions. Invoices are generated in structured XML or JSON, digitally signed and encrypted, and transmitted to ISTD for validation; only invoices processed through JoFotara or an integrated system are valid for tax deduction and accounting purposes.

name: Kazakhstan
keyDate: Mandatory B2B since 2019 (voluntary from 2014, mandatory for early taxpayer categories from 2017); expanded from 1 January 2026 to cover additional non-VAT-registered sectors
summary: Kazakhstan's Electronic Invoicing Information System (EIIS, also called IS ESF) is a centralised, government-run clearance platform for VAT invoices; direct exchange outside the platform is not permitted. Mandatory for domestic B2B since January 2019 (following a voluntary phase from 2014 and mandatory rollout for early taxpayer categories from 2017), e-invoices are the only valid basis for VAT deduction — paper invoices are not accepted for VAT credit. From 1 January 2026, the mandate expands to cover additional non-VAT-registered sectors, including international couriers, importers, forwarding agents, customs service providers, legal professionals and medical services.

name: Kenya
keyDate: TIMS deadline for VAT-registered taxpayers 30 September 2022 (extended from 31 July 2022); eTIMS extended to all businesses regardless of VAT status effective 1 September 2023 (Finance Act 2023); only eTIMS-generated invoices qualify for income-tax deductions from 1 January 2024
model: Clearance — real-time/near-real-time transmission and validation of invoice data through KRA
format: Local XML, via Electronic Tax Register (ETR)/OSCU/VSCU integration or the eTIMS platform; digital signature required
summary: Kenya's e-invoicing system evolved from Electronic Tax Registers (ETRs, since 2005) to the Tax Invoice Management System (TIMS, VAT-registered taxpayers required to comply by 30 September 2022, extended from an original 31 July 2022 deadline) and then to the cloud-based Electronic Tax Invoice Management System (eTIMS). The Finance Act 2023 extended the eTIMS requirement to all businesses regardless of VAT registration status, effective 1 September 2023, and from 1 January 2024 only expenses supported by valid eTIMS-generated electronic tax invoices qualify for income tax deductions. Kenya operates a clearance model requiring real-time invoice validation through KRA. A dedicated 'Reverse Invoicing' (self-billing) mechanism lets approved large buyers generate invoices on behalf of small-scale suppliers in structured supply chains (e.g. tea, coffee), via System-to-System Integration (OSCU/VSCU). Non-compliance can attract fines of up to KES 1 million, imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

name: Kiribati
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Ministry of Finance and Economic Development, Kiribati
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Kiribati in the sources reviewed. The Comarch source found for Kiribati is mistagged (content is about Israel's ITA e-invoicing specifications, not Kiribati) and was excluded. No Kiribati-specific evidence was found.

name: Kyrgyzstan
keyDate: Mandatory for goods suppliers since 2022 via ETTN; all taxpayers obliged to send/process electronic invoices via ETTN from 1 January 2023
model: CTC — invoices created, signed and submitted electronically to the tax authority and business partners via ETTN
summary: Kyrgyzstan mandates electronic invoicing via ETTN (Electronic Invoice Note system), operated by the Kyrgyzstan State Tax Service. The requirement began with the oil industry in May 2022, extended to goods suppliers generally later in 2022, and became mandatory for all taxpayers to send and process electronic invoices via ETTN from 1 January 2023. The system implements Continuous Transaction Controls (CTC), in line with a regional trend already seen in other former Soviet republics including Kazakhstan. Electronic signatures are mandatory.

name: Laos
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Lao PDR Ministry of Finance / Tax Department
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Laos in the sources reviewed. The official Lao Trade Portal source is a 2017 VAT law instruction with no e-invoicing content; no evidence of a mandate, platform, or proposal was found.

name: Latvia
keyDate: B2G e-invoicing mandatory since 1 Jan 2025; B2G/G2G e-invoice data reporting to SRS mandatory from 1 Jan 2026; B2B postponed from originally-planned 1 Jan 2026 to 1 January 2028
model: Exchange + reporting (Peppol BIS 3.0 / UBL 2.1); B2B still pending
format: Structured XML, UBL 2.1 and Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 compliant
authority: VID (Valsts ieņēmumu dienests / State Revenue Service, SRS)
summary: Latvia's e-invoicing rollout, part of its Shadow Economy Curtailment Plan (2024-2027), has B2G e-invoicing mandatory since 1 January 2025, with e-invoice data reporting to the State Revenue Service (SRS) for B2G/G2G transactions mandatory from 1 January 2026 under a Cabinet Regulation dated 9 December 2025. The originally-planned 1 January 2026 B2B mandate has been postponed to 1 January 2028, following the Latvian Parliament's adoption of a revised legislative framework in June 2025; voluntary B2B adoption is encouraged from 2026.

name: Lebanon
keyDate: No confirmed structured e-invoicing/CTC mandate or legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed; a related but distinct measure — mandatory electronic submission of all tax and administrative documents (income tax, salary tax, inheritance tax, VAT, real estate taxes) — took effect 6 October 2025
model: Not confirmed in sources reviewed — no structured e-invoicing platform or clearance/post-audit model identified
summary: Lebanon has no confirmed structured e-invoicing mandate as of the sources reviewed. Vendor commentary frames Lebanon as "watching closely" the regional e-invoicing wave (Saudi Arabia, Egypt, UAE, Jordan) and "expected to follow," but this is speculative — no specific law, decree, platform, or timeline was identified. A distinct and more concrete development is Lebanon's Ministry of Finance mandate, effective 6 October 2025, requiring electronic submission of all tax and administrative documents — covering income tax, salary tax, inheritance tax, VAT, and real estate taxes — as part of a broader administrative modernisation push. This is a tax-filing digitisation measure, not a structured business-to-business e-invoicing/CTC mandate, and should not be conflated with the kind of mandate seen in neighbouring Gulf states.

name: Lesotho
keyDate: Value Added Tax (E-Invoicing) Regulations, 2026 came into force 1 April 2026; mandatory go-live for VAT-registered businesses confirmed for 1 August 2026 — already in effect as of this dossier's date (10 August 2026)
model: Clearance-style — every sale, invoice, debit or credit note must pass through an Electronic Billing System (EBS) accredited by Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL), linked to the central Invoice Data Management System (IDMS)
format: Digitally signed invoices with QR code, linked to the central IDMS; specific XML/data schema not detailed in sources reviewed
summary: Lesotho has a mandatory, clearance-style e-invoicing regime that is now live. The Value Added Tax (E-Invoicing) Regulations, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026, and RSL confirmed 1 August 2026 as the mandatory go-live date for VAT-registered businesses — a date that has already passed as of this dossier. Under the regime, every VAT-registered vendor must issue invoices through an RSL-accredited Electronic Billing System (EBS); each invoice carries a digital signature and QR code linking it to the central Invoice Data Management System (IDMS). The system is not optional — a vendor cannot legally operate without an accredited EBS. Enforcement is strict: administrative penalties range from M50,000 to M300,000, with criminal sanctions of up to M500,000 in fines or six months' imprisonment. Lesotho joins Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, Egypt, Côte d'Ivoire, Angola and Cameroon among African jurisdictions using clearance-style e-invoicing or continuous transaction controls.

name: Liberia
keyDate: The Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) confirmed electronic invoicing is under development as a new feature of its Liberia Integrated Tax Administration System (LITAS), announced at LRA's first Digital Symposium on 15 April 2026 — no confirmed mandatory date, legal basis, or technical specification exists yet
model: Not yet defined — expected to build on LITAS (Liberia Integrated Tax Administration System), which already supports real-time registration, return filing, and payment
summary: Liberia has no e-invoicing mandate yet, but the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) has explicitly confirmed that electronic invoicing is under active development. At LRA's first Digital Symposium (Paynesville, 15 April 2026), held as part of Taxpayer Appreciation Month 2026, Assistant Commissioner for the Management Information Systems Division Kollie U. Zayzay stated that new services — including electronic invoicing and VAT features — are being developed within LITAS (Liberia Integrated Tax Administration System), the platform that already allows taxpayers to register, file returns, generate payment slips, and make payments in real time. This builds on a broader digital tax infrastructure that already includes ASYCUDA for customs, electronic fiscal devices monitoring transactions in real time, online tax clearance certificates, and digital verification tools. No confirmed mandatory date, legal basis, or technical specification for e-invoicing itself was identified in the sources reviewed.

name: Liechtenstein
keyDate: B2G reception mandatory since 10 November 2017
authority: Ministry of General Government Affairs and Finance
summary: Liechtenstein has a limited B2G e-invoicing obligation under which public contracting authorities must accept and process electronic invoices compliant with EN 16931 for public procurement contracts above the thresholds set in the national Public Procurement Act. There is no B2B or B2C mandate, and no centralised platform exists: invoices are submitted by email in XML or PDF format. No VAT real-time reporting or CTC system has been announced.

name: Lithuania
keyDate: B2G mandatory since Jul 2017 (SABIS from mid-2024); B2B mandate targeted for 2028
model: Centralised platform (SABIS) + Peppol network; post-audit for B2B
authority: Ministry of the Economy; State Tax Inspectorate (VMI)
summary: Lithuania has operated a mandatory B2G e-invoicing regime since 1 July 2017, delivered through the SABIS platform (which replaced eSąskaita from mid-2024) via the Peppol network and EN 16931-compliant formats. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, with no enacted legislation; the government has signalled an intention to introduce a B2B mandate targeting 2028, reusing the SABIS and Peppol infrastructure, but no statute has been published. The i.MAS system (comprising i.SAF, i.VAZ and i.SAF-T) operates as a separate, live digital reporting obligation for VAT and transport data.

Luxembourg is expected to await EU ViDA timelines for any future B2B mandate.

summary: Madagascar is developing a comprehensive, universal e-invoicing mandate under the 2024 Amended Finance Law (Draft Law No. 012/2024, adopted June 2024), which initiated the creation of an online invoicing module for a centralised, structured national e-invoicing platform. Unlike phased rollouts seen in many other countries, Madagascar's mandate is planned to apply to all taxpayers regardless of size or sector, and to all transaction types (B2B, B2C, B2G), from the outset. Decree No. 2025-738 has since advanced implementation, but the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) has not yet published final technical specifications or a confirmed effective date; earlier expectations of a 2025 launch have not materialised as of this dossier. In March 2026, Madagascar's DGI signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) to receive technology transfer and share expertise on Rwanda's mature Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) system, suggesting the platform is still being actively built rather than imminently launching.

name: Malawi
keyDate: Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) officially launched, replacing Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFD) introduced in 2014; final transition deadline moved to 1 May 2026 after three extensions (originally November 2025), with EFDs discontinued after 30 April 2026
model: Software-based fiscal invoicing — real-time submission of invoice data to the Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA) via the web-based EIS platform
format: Web-based software system (successor to hardware Electronic Fiscal Devices)
summary: Malawi has transitioned from hardware-based Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs), introduced in 2014, to a new web-based Electronic Invoicing System (EIS), administered by the Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA). After a pilot phase (extended from an original 1 February-cutoff to run through 30 April 2026 in response to taxpayer feedback) and three deadline extensions (moving the final cutoff from November 2025 to 1 May 2026), MRA officially launched EIS, discontinuing EFD use after 30 April 2026. More than 7,500 of the roughly 9,000 VAT-registered businesses had adopted the new system as of the rollout announcement. The VAT registration threshold was simultaneously raised from 25 million to 50 million Malawian kwacha, exempting smaller traders. The rollout faced resistance from some traders over privacy concerns and business closures in protest, prompting MRA to set up a support hotline, in-person centres, and nationwide training sessions.

name: Malaysia

summary: MyInvois clearance is rolling out in revenue-based waves since August 2024, reaching smaller businesses through 2025–2026 (micro-businesses exempted below RM500k). Near-real-time validation covers B2B, B2C and B2G transactions.

name: Maldives

model: Under consideration — expected to align with a Continuous Transaction Control approach, with invoice data reported to MIRA in real or near-real time through secure system integrations

summary: The Maldives Inland Revenue Authority (MIRA) is actively developing an e-invoicing system as the next phase of its tax administration digital transformation, though no mandatory legal requirement exists yet. Preliminary research and model selection began in mid-2025, and MIRA has publicly stated an intent to complete the system within 2026, aligning with international standards. In June 2026, MIRA formally launched an Asian Development Bank (ADB)-funded e-invoicing mission focused on integrating Regulatory Technology into tax administration, aimed at automating tax compliance, reducing tax evasion, and modernising services. MIRA is already highly digitised — 94-99% of tax statements/payments are submitted online — and views e-invoicing as a foundational capability for a broader shift toward real-time data, system integration, and embedded compliance, modelled loosely on OECD Tax Administration 3.0 principles. No confirmed mandatory date, specific legal instrument, or published technical format was found in the sources reviewed.

name: Mali
keyDate: No confirmed e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed; the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) has a modern digital tax administration (E-Quitus, e-impôt, electronic stamp-duty payment from 1 July 2026) but none of these systems constitute structured e-invoicing
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Mali in the sources reviewed, despite the country's prior 'proposed' classification. Mali's Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) — recognised as the country's best-digitalised administration during Mali's 2026 Digital Week — operates several genuine digital tax tools: E-Quitus (electronic tax clearance certificates, with a dedicated user manual), e-impôt (an online portal supporting financial-statement submission), and, from 1 July 2026, electronic payment of stamp duty on tax clearance certificates (Instruction N°2026-001/MEF-SG). None of these constitute structured, invoice-level e-invoicing or a Continuous Transaction Control system, and no source described such a system, a specific legislative proposal, or a timeline for one. Given the absence of supporting evidence, this dossier flags the prior 'proposed' status as unconfirmed rather than either fabricating a mandate narrative or unilaterally downgrading it.

There is no mandate for suppliers to issue e-invoices, and no B2B or B2C obligation exists. The MTCA has signalled interest in future mandatory e-invoicing and digital real-time reporting aligned with the EU ViDA timeline, but no concrete implementation dates have been confirmed.

The first phase is intended to apply to businesses above a turnover threshold, with a pre-clearance model proposed whereby invoices require tax authority approval before issuance to customers. No confirmed legal instrument, effective date, or technical format standard has been identified in the available sources.

name: Mauritius
keyDate: VAT e-Invoicing Regulations effective from 2 August 2022; Phase 1 (EBS developer/solution provider registration) live since 26 June 2023; Phase 2 (economic operator onboarding) began in stages from early 2024, initially targeting taxpayers with annual turnover above Rs 100 million; Phase 3 (mandatory issuance) rolling out progressively
model: Fiscalisation/clearance — sellers transmit invoice data via an Electronic Billing System (EBS) to the MRA's Invoice Fiscalisation Platform (IFP) in real time before issuing to the buyer
format: API-based transmission between EBS and IFP; specific document format not confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: Mauritius is introducing a national e-Invoicing system in a phased approach, administered by the Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA) under Value Added Tax e-Invoicing Regulations effective 2 August 2022 (introduced by the Minister of Finance on 18 September 2023, amended by the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2022). Providers of goods and services are required to fiscalise their invoices or receipts in real time with the MRA, via an Electronic Billing System (EBS) — the taxpayer's accounting package, invoicing solution, POS, ECR or ERP — connected by API to the MRA's Invoice Fiscalisation Platform (IFP). Phase 1 (software developer/solution provider registration and self-certification) has been live since 26 June 2023. Phase 2 (economic operator onboarding of compliant EBS) began in stages from early 2024, initially targeting taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding Rs 100 million, with further stages extending to smaller taxpayers over time. Phase 3 concerns mandatory issuance of fiscal invoices by economic operators. Each fiscalised invoice receives a unique QR code, enabling customers to independently verify that the transaction was reported to the MRA.

summary: CFDI covers effectively all invoicing, with certified providers (PACs) validating and digitally stamping documents before they reach SAT — among the most comprehensive e-invoicing regimes globally, in force since 2011 with no size or industry exemptions. A January 2026 tax reform strengthened authenticity requirements and SAT enforcement powers, and a new Rule 2.9.21 (effective 1 April 2026) goes beyond invoicing itself, requiring digital service providers and marketplace platforms to give SAT direct, real-time access to their transaction data.

name: Moldova
keyDate: e-Factura launched as a voluntary system in 2014; B2G mandatory since 2023; cross-border B2B exports added 2025; full mandatory B2B for all VAT-registered domestic transactions from 1 October 2026, following a January 2026 pilot

format: Standardized XML via e-Factura, embedded within SIA Cabinetul personal al contribuabilului (the taxpayer cabinet); moving toward Peppol/eDelivery interoperability
authority: State Tax Service (Serviciul Fiscal de Stat, SFS)
summary: Moldova is completing a decade-long transition from voluntary to mandatory e-invoicing via its national e-Factura platform, operated by the State Tax Service (SFS). Launched as a voluntary service in 2014, e-Factura became mandatory for B2G transactions in 2021/2023 (sources vary on the precise year), was extended to cross-border B2B exports in 2025, and will become mandatory for all domestic B2B transactions between VAT-registered entities from 1 October 2026, following a January 2026 pilot phase. The mandate operates as a comprehensive Continuous Transaction Control (CTC) framework: standardized, digitally-signed XML invoices are submitted in real time to the SFS platform, embedded within SIA Cabinetul personal al contribuabilului (the unified taxpayer cabinet) rather than a standalone e-invoicing website. A parallel e-receipt system (eBon, via Virtual Cash Registers) is being introduced for B2C retail transactions. Penalties for non-compliance are severe, ranging up to 25-35% of transaction value. Moldova, an EU candidate country since June 2022, is simultaneously pursuing Peppol/eDelivery interoperability, including EU-supported pilots for Moldova-Ukraine cross-border exchange.

name: Monaco
keyDate: From 1 September 2026, Monegasque VAT-registered entities (SIREN/SIRET-registered, or otherwise within the Monaco-France VAT territory) must comply with France's e-invoicing mandate: large/mid-sized companies must issue structured e-invoices, and every business regardless of size must be able to receive them; small/micro/medium companies follow from 1 September 2027
model: Follows France's e-invoicing framework — Public Invoicing Platform (PPF) or approved Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs); post-audit model per DDD Invoices' compliance-map summary
format: UBL, CII, or Factur-X, per France's Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP) framework
authority: Direction des Services Fiscaux (Monaco Department of Tax Services), operating within France's VAT territory
summary: Monaco is not an EU member state but shares a single VAT territory with France under a bilateral customs union and VAT agreement (Tax Treaty of 18 May 1963, as updated). Because of this, VAT-registered Monaco businesses are pulled directly into France's e-invoicing and e-reporting reform on the same national timeline: from 1 September 2026, large and mid-sized companies must issue structured e-invoices and report e-reporting data, and every business regardless of size must be able to receive e-invoices; from 1 September 2027, the issuance obligation extends to small, micro and medium-sized companies. As Monaco is outside the EU, it is not directly subject to the EU's ViDA framework (mandatory from 2030), but the France-aligned obligation applies regardless. As of this dossier's date (10 August 2026), the first deadline is about three weeks away and not yet in force, so this is classified as 'announced' rather than 'live'.

name: Mongolia
keyDate: eBarimt electronic VAT receipt system mandatory nationwide since 1 January 2016
model: Real-time electronic receipt — each VAT-relevant transaction is issued a structured, QR-coded electronic receipt registered with the tax authority at point of sale
format: Structured electronic receipt via certified POS/software connected to the eBarimt system; QR code + unique identifier per receipt
summary: Mongolia has a mandatory, real-time electronic VAT receipt system called eBarimt, operated by the General Department of Taxation and in force nationwide since 1 January 2016. Every VAT-relevant transaction must be issued as a structured electronic receipt (not a mandate on B2B invoices in the EN 16931/Peppol sense, but a mandatory fiscal-receipt regime functionally equivalent to e-invoicing for VAT purposes) through certified POS/software connected to the eBarimt system, each carrying a unique identifier and QR code. Consumers can register receipts via the eBarimt mobile app to claim a VAT cashback, which has driven strong organic compliance/adoption pressure from the demand side as well as the supply side. Input VAT credit for businesses is conditional on a matching eBarimt receipt. This was previously misclassified as 'none' after a research pass whose banked sources were mistagged to Chinese e-fapiao content rather than genuine Mongolia-specific material — corrected here based on verified, multi-source confirmation of eBarimt's mandatory, real-time operation.

name: Montenegro
keyDate: Real-time fiscalization mandatory since 1 January 2021 (full enforcement 1 June 2021) for all VAT-registered persons; separate structured B2B/B2G e-invoicing platform (to be adapted from Serbia's e-Faktura) not yet legislated as of July 2026, go-live speculative between 2025 and 2027
model: Live: CTC-type real-time fiscalization (digitally-signed XML invoice data sent to tax authority at issuance, IKOF/JIKR codes + QR code returned). Planned: structured B2B/B2G CTC e-invoicing platform adapted from Serbia's e-Faktura
format: Live: digitally-signed XML via certified software. Planned: OASIS UBL 2.1 / EN 16931, Peppol-aligned
authority: Ministarstvo Finansija (Ministry of Finance); Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore (Revenue and Customs Administration)
summary: Montenegro operates two distinct, related digital tax compliance systems. Real-time fiscalization has been mandatory since 1 January 2021 (fully enforced from 1 June 2021) under the Law on Fiscalization in the Turnover of Products and Services: every invoice — cash and non-cash, B2C, B2B and B2G — is transmitted to the Revenue and Customs Administration at the moment of issuance via certified software, receiving a unique JIKR code and QR code in real time. Separately, Montenegro is preparing a structured B2B/B2G e-invoicing platform intended to be adapted from Serbia's state-owned e-Faktura system (licensed to Montenegro free of charge through a multi-year agreement), targeting EN 16931/UBL 2.1 compliance and driven by Montenegro's EU accession ambitions. As of July 2026 this structured platform is not yet legislated, and its go-live date remains speculative, with estimates ranging from 2025 to 2027.

No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been identified from the official sources. The department's digital focus as of August 2026 is limited to a property tax online payment platform, with filing tax returns and a property tax calculator listed as coming soon.

name: Morocco
keyDate: Public consultation launched October 2024; pilot phase from October 2025; mandatory rollout begins early 2026 for ~1,655 large companies (turnover above MAD 200 million); gradual extension to SMEs and micro-businesses in 2027-2028
model: Clearance — invoices must be pre-validated (cleared) by the DGI before being legally valid
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) — General Directorate of Taxes
summary: Morocco's e-invoicing mandate is built on Article 145-9 of the General Tax Code (Code Général des Impôts, CGI), introduced via the 2018 Loi de Finances, which provided for electronic handling of invoices and accounting records. The DGI relaunched the initiative with a public consultation in October 2024, ran a pilot phase from October 2025, and mandatory implementation begins in early 2026, per the 2026 Finance Bill (PLF 2026). The first phase covers approximately 1,655 large companies with turnover above MAD 200 million; a gradual extension to SMEs and micro-businesses is planned for 2027-2028. Under the clearance model, every business must issue invoices electronically in UBL 2.1 format and obtain DGI clearance before the invoice is legally valid. xHub, a Moroccan software engineering firm, has been selected as the technology partner developing the national e-invoicing platform. As of the sources reviewed, the government has not yet published a comprehensive implementing decree covering every technical detail (format specifics, electronic signatures, full scope) — these remain subject to further decrees and technical regulations still to be released.

name: Mozambique
keyDate: Mandatory monthly electronic submission of VAT invoice data has applied since May 2025 (Notice No. /AT/DGI/2025 of 27 March 2025); SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) implementation preparation is underway, with software developers required to obtain technical specifications from the Mozambique Tax Authority
model: Structured monthly e-reporting — VAT taxpayers extract invoice data from MTA-certified billing software and upload a compressed file via the MTA's electronic declaration platform (e-declaração)
format: Compressed data file extracted from certified invoicing software; SAF-T format implementation in preparation
authority: Autoridade Tributária de Moçambique (Mozambique Tax Authority, MTA), via the Directorate General of Taxation (DGI)
summary: Mozambique operates a mandatory structured e-reporting regime for VAT invoices, not yet a full real-time clearance system. Since a Tax Authority Notice dated 27 March 2025 (Notice No. /AT/DGI/2025), all VAT taxpayers must submit a monthly file to the Mozambique Tax Authority (MTA) containing data on every invoice issued for the preceding month's operations, effective from May 2025 filings (covering April 2025 transactions), under Article 27(10) of the VAT Code (introduced by a 2016 amendment). Invoice data must be extracted from MTA-certified invoicing software (certification governed by a Ministerial Order of 29 February 2012) and uploaded as a compressed file via the MTA's e-declaração electronic declaration platform. Separately, the MTA is preparing to implement the OECD Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T), requiring accounting/invoicing software developers to obtain the SAF-T technical data-structure specifications and undergo certification. Failure to submit the required monthly invoice file carries legal penalties.

name: Namibia
keyDate: First announced in the 2024/25 national budget; originally targeted for an April 2026 fixed-date rollout, revised in the 2026/27 budget statement to a phased implementation spanning the 2026/27-2028/29 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, with no confirmed enforcement dates as of this dossier

The Namibian government, through the Ministry of Finance and the Namibia Revenue Agency (NamRA), is firmly committed to introducing a comprehensive VAT e-invoicing regime, first announced in the 2024/25 national budget and reaffirmed by NamRA in March 2025 with an initial fixed target of April 2026. The 2026/27 national budget statement officially removed that fixed deadline, repositioning the mandate as part of a broader administrative and tax policy reform package spanning the 2026/27-2028/29 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework — a shift toward a gradual, three-year phased implementation rather than a single-date launch. The future system will operate on a centralised clearance model, requiring VAT-registered businesses (local and foreign) to transmit invoice data to NamRA's Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) in near real-time, covering most domestic B2B, B2C (including cash registers), and B2G transactions.

summary: Nepal is phasing in mandatory e-invoicing, administered by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD). A narrower fiscal billing system, the Central Billing Monitoring System (CBMS), has applied to fraud-susceptible industries since 2017. Nepal's 2024-25 Budget introduced mandatory e-invoicing for all businesses, with implementation beginning 16 July 2024 for businesses with annual transactions exceeding NPR 250 million; the regime involves pre-clearance and direct exchange of invoicing information with IRD. Businesses generally in scope include VAT-registered and PAN-registered taxpayers, those with turnover exceeding NPR 5 million, and specific mandated industries (electronics, medicine, FMCG, wholesalers, retailers, manufacturers, importers/distributors). The technical and procedural framework is set out in the Electronic Billing Procedure, 2074 (most recently the 4th amendment, published 5 October 2021), covering billing equipment/software approval and cloud-based computing requirements.

name: Niger
keyDate: Certified electronic invoicing (SECeF) mandatory for all VAT-registered companies since 1 September 2021, per the Finance Laws of 2020 and 2021; progressive rollout starting with large companies and priority sectors
model: Clearance — invoice transmitted to DGI's SECeF system at issuance via an approved SFE + MCF combination, which checks, records and certifies it before it is valid
summary: Niger mandates certified electronic invoicing via SECeF (Système Électronique Certifié de Facturation), administered by the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI). Since 1 September 2021, per the Finance Laws of 2020 and 2021, all VAT-registered companies under both the standard and simplified real tax regimes must issue certified electronic invoices. The system relies on two components — an approved SFE (Enterprise Invoicing System, the company's invoicing software) and an MCF (Invoicing Control Module, which certifies each invoice) — combined into an Invoicing Unit (UF). Every invoice carries a unique identifier, fiscal seal (SECeF/DGI code) and QR code, requires a mandatory electronic signature, and must be archived for 10 years per Article 358 of the Code Général des Impôts (General Tax Code). An invoice not certified by the DGI system is not legally valid.

format: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 UBL (XML or JSON)
summary: Nigeria's Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) has rolled out the Merchant-Buyer Solution (FIRSMBS), a national e-invoicing platform, under legal authority granted by the FIRS Establishment Act 2007 (Section 25: administer tax laws; Section 26: deploy technology to automate tax processes/assessments/audits). A pilot began in late 2024, with mandatory compliance for large taxpayers taking effect 1 November 2025, covering B2B and B2G structured e-invoicing plus real-time e-reporting for B2C sales exceeding NGN 50,000. Medium and small VAT-registered businesses are expected to enter mandatory compliance from 1 January 2026, broadening the regime beyond large corporations. Non-resident suppliers are currently excluded but authorities are anticipated to revisit this scope during 2026. The system adopts Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 UBL formats (XML or JSON) for interoperability, with businesses integrating either directly via API or through Accredited Access Point Providers (APPs) authorised under National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) standards.

name: Niue
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Niue Tax Office, Niue Ministry of Finance
summary: Niue has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme as of August 2026. The Niue Tax Office administers income tax, PAYE, and the Niue Consumption Tax through an online filing portal, but invoicing itself remains entirely paper or commercially discretionary. No legal instrument, pilot, or policy proposal relating to e-invoicing has been identified in any official source.

name: Norfolk Island
keyDate: Follows Australia's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Norfolk Island does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows Australia's regime directly. Australian tax and superannuation law has applied on Norfolk Island since 1 July 2016, administered directly by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) — the same authority and framework as mainland Australia, though GST, luxury car tax, wine equalisation tax and fuel tax credits are exempted locally. See the Australia dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: North Macedonia
keyDate: e-Faktura pilot launched 5 January 2026; three testing phases run through mid-2026; full production and mandatory rollout for all VAT-registered businesses from 1 October 2026, with no official grace period
model: Clearance — centralised Continuous Transaction Control (CTC); e-invoices submitted to the Public Revenue Office's central platform for validation, which assigns a unique electronic identifier (eID) before the document is visible to both parties
authority: Public Revenue Office (PRO / Управа за јавни приходи)
summary: North Macedonia's Public Revenue Office (PRO) is rolling out e-Faktura, a centralised Continuous Transaction Control e-invoicing system that will apply to nearly all B2B, B2G, and some B2C transactions. B2G has been mandatory under public procurement rules aligned with EU Directive 2014/55/EU since 2025. The PRO launched the e-Faktura pilot on 5 January 2026 and has run it through successive testing phases (API/ERP integration, expanded tax-indicator functionality, and a web-based testing app for all taxpayers), with roughly 200 companies and 30 educational sessions involved by the third phase (June 2026). Full mandatory e-invoicing for all VAT-registered domestic and foreign businesses takes effect 1 October 2026, with no official grace period; paper and PDF invoices will no longer be accepted from that date. Non-compliance, late transmission, or incorrect data can trigger fines ranging from €300 to €10,000.

name: Northern Mariana Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Division of Revenue and Taxation, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands
summary: The Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) operates its own tax administration through the Division of Revenue and Taxation, with an income tax system based partly on the US Internal Revenue Code and partly on local CNMI law. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, pilot programme, or credible legislative proposal has been identified in any available official source. The CNMI profile therefore remains at status none as of August 2026.

name: Norway
keyDate: Stortinget (Parliament) officially approved mandatory B2B e-invoicing legislation June 2026; mandatory issuance from 1 January 2027 (asymmetric — only if buyer is ELMA/Peppol-registered); mandatory reception + automated digital bookkeeping from 1 January 2030
model: Peppol-based exchange, via the EHF format (a Peppol BIS 3.0 implementation aligned with EN 16931); ELMA registry integrated into the Peppol directory
format: EHF (Elektronisk Handelsformat) — Norway's Peppol BIS 3.0 implementation; primary legislation is technologically neutral, requiring only a 'structured, standardized, and machine-readable electronic format'
authority: Skatteetaten / Skattedirektoratet (Norwegian Tax Administration); Ministry of Finance
summary: In June 2026, the Norwegian Parliament (Stortinget) officially approved legislation introducing mandatory B2B e-invoicing and digital bookkeeping, following a March 2026 government letter and a public consultation process. The mandate rolls out in two phases with a deliberately asymmetric structure: from 1 January 2027, all businesses with bookkeeping obligations in Norway must issue e-invoices to any business counterparty registered in the Electronic Recipient Register (ELMA, now integrated into the Peppol directory) — but buyers have no obligation to receive e-invoices until 1 January 2030, when mandatory reception and automated digital-accounting capability also take effect. The practical technical standard will be EHF (Elektronisk Handelsformat), Norway's existing, dominant e-invoice format (89% of e-invoice volume per Norges Bank 2020) — itself a Peppol BIS 3.0 implementation fully aligned with EN 16931 — though the primary legislation itself remains technology-neutral. Exemptions are planned for micro-businesses under NOK 50,000 annual turnover and specific regulated sectors (bankruptcy estates, financial enterprises, banks, insurers, pension funds). The bill still requires Royal Assent, and Skattedirektoratet must publish detailed technical regulations (forskrift) by 15 December 2026 at the latest.

name: Oman
keyDate: Mandatory B2B from April 2027 (large taxpayers above OMR 5 million)
summary: Oman's Fawtara e-invoicing programme gained its legal foundation on 9 August 2026 when the Oman Tax Authority issued Decision No. 189/2026, replacing Article 143 of the VAT Executive Regulations and setting a phased mandatory B2B obligation. Taxable persons with annual supplies above OMR 5 million must comply from 1 April 2027, with all remaining VAT-registered taxpayers following from 1 October 2027. The system operates on a decentralised five-corner Peppol model using the PINT OM format, with a voluntary pilot of approximately 100 selected large companies running from August 2026.

name: Pakistan
keyDate: Phased live rollout from September 2025; all registered persons by December 2025
summary: Pakistan operates a mandatory centralised clearance e-invoicing system administered by the Federal Board of Revenue, under which notified taxpayers must integrate their ERP or POS systems with the FBR IRIS platform via licensed integrators for real-time invoice validation. The rollout is phased by taxpayer category and turnover, with large taxpayers and importers live from September 2025 and all remaining registered persons required by December 2025. Each validated invoice receives a unique Invoice Reference Number, UUID, and QR code from the FBR before it may be legally issued.
