(Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Panama
keyDate: Broad mandatory rollout ongoing; PAC threshold tightened Jan 2026
summary: Panama operates the Sistema de Factura Electrónica de Panamá (SFEP), under which taxpayers must issue digitally signed XML invoices (Comprobantes Fiscales Electrónicos) validated and authorised in real time by a DGI-certified provider known as a PAC. The legal framework rests primarily on Law 256 of 2021 and Executive Decree 766 of 2020, with subsequent resolutions progressively expanding the mandatory scope to cover most taxpayers. From 1 January 2026, only taxpayers with annual gross revenues up to B/. 36,000 and issuing no more than 100 documents per month may use the DGI free invoicing tool; all others must use a certified PAC.

name: Papua New Guinea
keyDate: No confirmed e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed; the Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) has digitised tax payments (myIRC online portal, since 2022) and is implementing the new Income Tax Act 2025 (effective 1 January 2026), but neither directly establishes structured e-invoicing
model: Not confirmed in sources reviewed — no e-invoicing model identified; standard manual GST tax invoices remain the norm under existing IRC rules
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Papua New Guinea in the sources reviewed, despite the country's prior 'proposed' classification. The Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) has digitised parts of its tax administration — notably the myIRC online payment portal (established around 2022, built with partner Niupay on AWS infrastructure) and standard GST tax invoice content requirements (a fixed checklist including TIN, invoice number, GST at 10%, and buyer TIN for invoices over PGK 1,000) — and is implementing the new Income Tax Act 2025 (effective 1 January 2026), which modernises tax identification and registration processes. However, none of the sources reviewed describe a structured, invoice-level e-invoicing platform, a clearance or CTC model, or any specific timeline for introducing one. IRC's stated strategic priorities focus on revenue growth, enforcement, audits, and interoperability across existing systems, with digital reporting infrastructure discussed only in general terms.

name: Paraguay
keyDate: Decree 872/2023 effective 1 January 2024 (superseding earlier regulation); mandatory implementation calendar (2021) covered 8 taxpayer groups from January 2023 to October 2024; General Resolution 21/2024 phased in medium/large taxpayers from 3 March 2025; SIFEN mandatory for government suppliers/contractors/consultants from 2 January 2026 (General Resolution DNIT No. 41/2025)
model: Clearance — tax documents (DTE) acquire operational validity only after passing DNIT's technical validation controls via SIFEN
format: XML with digital signature, via e-Kuatia (medium/large taxpayers) or e-Kuatia'i (small taxpayers)
summary: Paraguay operates SIFEN (Sistema Integrado de Facturación Electrónica Nacional), a mandatory clearance-model e-invoicing system administered by the Dirección Nacional de Ingresos Tributarios (DNIT). Tax documents (Documentos Tributarios Electrónicos, DTE) — issued in structured XML with a digital signature — acquire legal validity only after passing DNIT's technical validation. A 2021 mandatory implementation calendar phased in 8 taxpayer groups between January 2023 and October 2024; Decree 872/2023 (effective 1 January 2024) further regulated the regime and added new DTE document types; General Resolution 21/2024 phased in additional medium and large taxpayers from 3 March 2025. From 2 January 2026, SIFEN adoption became mandatory for suppliers, contractors and consultants entering contracts with entities covered by public procurement regulations, per General Resolution DNIT No. 41/2025. DNIT reports more than 2 billion DTEs received through SIFEN to date, with documented cost savings of 30-75% on issuance, 40-80% on reception, 90-100% on distribution (courier), and 30-50% on storage.

name: Peru
keyDate: CPE electronic receipts universal across taxpayer segments; SUNAT Resolution 000075-2026 (effective 1 June 2026) ties e-invoicing obligation to RUC registration/regime changes; SIRE deadline for Principal Taxpayers (PRICOS) postponed from June 2026 to October 2026
summary: Peru's Comprobante de Pago Electrónico (CPE) system is mandatory across taxpayer segments via SUNAT's Electronic Issuance System (SEE) or authorised Electronic Service Operators (OSE). SUNAT Resolution No. 000075-2026, effective 1 June 2026, ties the start of mandatory e-invoicing to the date of RUC (taxpayer registry) registration for certain tax regimes, and to regime-exit dates for others, while expanding Integrated Electronic Records System (SIRE) obligations. A subsequent update postponed the SIRE deadline for Principal Taxpayers (PRICOS) from June 2026 to October 2026.

name: Philippines
keyDate: Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) mandated by Revenue Regulation No. 11-2025 (25 Feb 2025); Stage 1 rollout began March 2026 for large taxpayers/e-commerce/digital platforms, with enforceable obligation extended to 31 December 2026; Stage 2 (exporters, incentivized enterprises, POS retailers) expected later in 2027, BIR-readiness dependent
model: Structured e-reporting (not real-time clearance) — invoices transmitted to BIR's EIS platform for near-real-time exchange; seller-buyer transmission itself remains unregulated (can be paper/PDF/any format)
format: JSON, via BIR-approved software, integrating with BIR systems
summary: The Philippines' Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) introduced a mandatory e-invoicing framework via Revenue Regulation No. 11-2025 (25 February 2025), building on a 2022-2023 pilot program and the original legal basis in the TRAIN Law (Republic Act No. 10963). The Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) is a centralised digital platform requiring eligible taxpayers to issue and transmit Sales Invoices, Official Receipts, Service Billings, and Debit/Credit Notes using BIR-approved software in JSON format. Stage 1 rollout began March 2026 for high-volume/priority taxpayers (large taxpayers, e-commerce/digital platform businesses, corporations with annual sales over PHP 1 billion, users of BIR-approved computerized books), with the enforceable compliance deadline subsequently extended to 31 December 2026 to give affected taxpayers more preparation time. Stage 2, expected later in 2027 and dependent on BIR system readiness, extends the mandate to exporters, incentivized enterprises, POS-based retailers, and other BIR-designated groups. Notably, the Philippines model is a structured e-reporting system, not a real-time clearance regime: invoice transmission between seller and buyer itself remains unregulated (can still be paper or PDF), while a separate, parallel transmission to BIR is what's mandated.

name: Pitcairn Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Government of the Pitcairn Islands (Island Council)
summary: Pitcairn Islands is a British Overseas Territory with a resident population of approximately fifty people. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, programme, or legislative framework relating to electronic invoicing has been identified in any available official source. The territory's administrative scale makes a formal e-invoicing regime neither present nor foreseeable.

name: Poland
keyDate: Live: large taxpayers Feb 2026, all VAT businesses Apr 2026, micro Jan 2027
format: FA_VAT XML (based on EN 16931), also called the FA(3) schema
summary: Poland's mandatory B2B e-invoicing system, KSeF (Krajowy System e-Faktur), went live on 1 February 2026 for businesses with prior-year sales exceeding PLN 200 million, and extended to all other VAT-registered businesses on 1 April 2026. Invoices must be submitted to the KSeF platform for clearance before they are considered valid; an 11-month penalty-free soft-landing period applies during the initial onboarding phases. Digitally excluded micro-taxpayers with individual invoices up to PLN 450 and monthly sales up to PLN 10,000 must comply from 1 January 2027. KSeF 1.0 was permanently discontinued on 1 February 2026 in favour of KSeF 2.0, and mandatory KSeF identifiers in bank transfer payment references take effect 1 August 2026.

name: Portugal
keyDate: B2G live (CIUS-PT); B2B/B2C not mandated for structured e-invoicing. QES requirement for PDF invoices delayed to 1 January 2027; SAF-T submission delayed to 2028
summary: Portugal mandates B2G e-invoicing in CIUS-PT format, and requires an ATCUD code (via certified software) and QR code on invoices generally, but domestic B2B/B2C structured e-invoicing remains voluntary. Two separate, long-delayed obligations continue to slip: the Qualified Electronic Signature (QES) requirement for PDF invoices, originally due 1 July 2021, has been postponed repeatedly and now takes effect 1 January 2027 (per law 37/XVII/1, voted December 2025); mandatory SAF-T file submission, originally set for 2026, has similarly slipped to 2028.

name: Puerto Rico

authority: Departamento de Hacienda de Puerto Rico
summary: Puerto Rico operates its own independent tax administration under the Departamento de Hacienda and levies a Sales and Use Tax (IVU) at a combined rate of 11.5 percent, administered digitally through the SURI portal. No e-invoicing mandate, structured B2B or B2G e-invoicing programme, or credible announcement of one has been identified in the available sources. The SURI portal obligation covers tax-return filing and merchant registration, not structured invoice exchange between trading parties.

The final technical specifications, taxpayer scope, format requirements, and mandatory go-live date have not yet been published by the GTA. Businesses should begin readiness assessments but should not rely on any specific implementation date or model that has not been officially confirmed.

name: Romania
keyDate: B2G since 2016; B2B mandatory since July 2024; B2C mandatory via RO e-Factura since January 2025; unified 5-working-day transmission deadline from January 2026
summary: All domestic B2B invoices in Romania flow through the RO e-Factura clearance platform, mandatory since July 2024, with B2C reporting added via the same system from January 2025. Government Emergency Ordinance 89/2025 (23 December 2025) unified the transmission deadline for both B2B and B2C invoices to 5 working days from January 2026 (previously 5 calendar days for B2B, undefined for B2C), clarified that B2B invoices to non-established-but-VAT-identified buyers must still route through RO e-Factura, and introduced a new registration requirement for individual entrepreneurs (using their personal CNP identifier) before starting economic activity.

name: Russia
keyDate: Mandatory for traceable goods from 1 July 2021; mandatory B2G federal contracts from 1 April 2024
summary: Russia operates a live e-invoicing regime anchored by the Universal Transfer Document (UPD) and a network of FNS-accredited Electronic Document Management operators. E-invoicing is mandatory for taxpayers dealing in traceable goods (from 1 July 2021) and for federal government contract supply (from 1 April 2024), while general B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary but is heavily adopted. Plans to extend a full mandatory B2B mandate were suspended by the Ministry of Finance in June 2022 and no new target date is confirmed in the available sources.

name: Rwanda
keyDate: Electronic Invoicing System (EIS/EBM) mandatory since 1 January 2021; 'EBM for All' income-tax validation policy announced December 2020; Tax Procedure law of 2023 extends the EBM requirement to all persons carrying out taxable activities, VAT-registered or not
model: Certified device/software issuance with real-time data transmission to RRA (Electronic Billing Machine — EBM)
format: EBM-generated invoice via one of five certified methods (software, mobile/SMS app, online solution, Online Sales Data Controller, or Virtual Sales Data Controller), transmitted via API
summary: Rwanda's Electronic Invoicing System (EIS), built on Electronic Billing Machines (EBM), has been mandatory since 1 January 2021 for every sales transaction, B2B and B2C. Registered taxpayers must generate certified invoices in real time via one of five RRA-approved methods and transmit data to RRA via API. The Tax Procedure law of 2023 extended the EBM-issuance requirement to every person carrying out taxable activities, regardless of VAT registration status; failure to comply is a tax crime. The 'EBM for All' policy, announced December 2020, added income-tax validation requirements using EBM receipts, pushing large firms to demand electronic invoices from suppliers and creating strong formalisation pressure on small businesses. VAT registration is required above FRW 20,000,000 annual turnover (or FRW 5,000,000 in a preceding quarter), though EBM issuance itself applies more broadly under the 2023 law. Non-compliance penalties are steep: up to 20x the evaded VAT (or fixed fines up to 400,000 RWF for non-VAT-registered taxpayers) for repeat offences, plus business closure of up to 30 days and public-tender debarment.

name: San Marino
keyDate: E-invoicing mandatory since 2022 for the trade of goods and services between San Marino and Italy via the Sistema di Interscambio (SDI); no blanket domestic mandate for purely internal San Marino-to-San Marino transactions
model: Clearance — invoices transmitted via Italy's SDI (Sistema di Interscambio) for the San Marino-Italy cross-border scope
format: XML; FatturaPA for the Italy-linked SDI route, XML-RSM format for the San Marino-specific cross-border variant
authority: San Marino Segreteria di Stato per le Finanze e il Bilancio (Ministry of Finance and Budget) / Tax Office
summary: San Marino has a live, mandatory e-invoicing regime, but it is narrowly and specifically scoped to cross-border trade in goods and services with Italy, not a blanket domestic mandate. Since 2021, San Marino joined the Italian e-invoicing model via the cross-border Sistema di Interscambio (SDI); since 2022, e-invoicing became mandatory for the trade of goods and services between San Marino and Italy, per Delegated Decree No. 163 of 20 September 2021 (ratifying Delegated Decree No. 148 of 5 August 2021) and Regulation No. 14 of 8 September 2021. Invoices use XML format (FatturaPA for standard SDI transmission, or the XML-RSM format specific to San Marino-Italy trade), covering B2B transactions primarily. Purely domestic transactions among San Marino operators are explicitly NOT covered by this mandate — the Italian Revenue Agency's own ruling (Risposta n. 58/2024) confirms the SDI framework applies only to cross-border San Marino-Italy goods flows, not internal San Marino relationships.

name: Saudi Arabia
keyDate: Phase 1 live Dec 2021; Phase 2 Wave 25 requires integration by 1 Feb 2027 for taxpayers above SAR 187,500 (2022-2025 revenue)
summary: Saudi Arabia's FATOORA e-invoicing system is fully operational. Phase 1, requiring all VAT-registered taxpayers to generate structured electronic invoices, has been mandatory since December 2021. Phase 2, which adds mandatory API integration with ZATCA's FATOORA platform for real-time clearance, has rolled out in over 24 revenue-based waves since January 2023 and by 1 February 2027, SAR 187,500 threshold (Wave 25) covers businesses with annual VATable revenue above SAR 375,000.

name: Senegal
keyDate: 2025 Finance Bill ends the voluntary status e-invoicing has held since 2008, making electronic invoicing mandatory for all taxable entities; no official implementation timeline had been released as of the sources reviewed
model: Not yet finalised — invoices must be submitted in a structured electronic format via either a public invoicing portal or another authority-designated digital platform; exact format and platform not yet specified
format: Structured electronic format — specific standard not yet specified; Benin's e-MECeF (structured JSON files to a centralised platform) referenced as a potential model
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines (DGID)
summary: Senegal's Directorate General of Taxes and Domains (DGID) is transitioning e-invoicing from a voluntary option (permitted since 2008 under the General Tax Code but never centrally systemised, resulting in limited adoption) to a mandatory regime, via the 2025 Finance Bill. The new legislation applies to all taxable entities and requires invoices to be submitted in a structured electronic format through either a public invoicing portal or another digital platform designated by the authorities; the exact technical format has not been specified, though Senegal has looked to neighbouring Benin's e-MECeF system (structured JSON files to a centralised platform) as a potential model. Non-compliance — failing to issue, transmit, or receive electronic invoices — carries fines of 25% of the VAT that should have been invoiced electronically, capped at XOF 5 million (approximately EUR 7,700) per invoice. No official implementation timeline had been released as of the sources reviewed.

name: Serbia
keyDate: B2G issue mandatory from 1 May 2022; B2G receive from 1 Jul 2022; B2B mandatory from 1 Jan 2023
format: UBL 2.1, qualified electronic signature and/or secure electronic channel
summary: Serbia rolled out mandatory e-invoicing in three phases via the national SEF (Sistem E-Faktura) platform: public-sector suppliers had to issue e-invoices to government from 1 May 2022, public entities had to be able to send e-invoices to companies from 1 July 2022, and B2B e-invoicing became mandatory economy-wide from 1 January 2023. Non-compliance carries a fine of around €17,000. Invoices are stored via the ancillary Sistem za Upravljanje Fakturama (SUF).

name: Seychelles
keyDate: Cabinet approved introduction of an electronic invoicing system (announced 8 February 2024); procurement formally began March 2026 with publication of an Expression of Interest; Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) entered the final stage of e-invoicing procurement as of 25 July 2026 — system not yet implemented
model: Automatic real-time transfer of billing information between businesses and the tax authority (per Cabinet's description); technical model not yet finalised pending procurement outcome
format: Not yet confirmed — pending procurement of the Electronic Invoicing Solution (EIS)
summary: Seychelles has a Cabinet-approved plan for mandatory electronic invoicing, first announced in February 2024 as part of budget reforms to improve tax compliance and reduce revenue leakage, initially covering VAT with other taxes to be added in stages. The Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) issued a formal Expression of Interest for a 'Consultancy Services for the Supply and Implementation of an Electronic Invoicing Solution (EIS)' with a December 2025 submission deadline, and as of 25 July 2026 SRC confirmed it has entered the final stage of procurement — but the system itself has not yet been implemented. This is a genuine, government-committed initiative moving through a lengthy but real procurement pipeline, not yet a live or technically-specified mandate.

summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Sierra Leone in the sources reviewed. name: Singapore
keyDate: Mandatory for all new voluntary GST registrants from 1 April 2026; full rollout to all GST-registered businesses by April 2031
format: Peppol PINT SG (replacing SG Peppol BIS Billing 3.0)
summary: Singapore is phasing in mandatory GST invoice data transmission via the InvoiceNow network (Peppol-based). The GST InvoiceNow Requirement applies progressively: newly incorporated voluntary GST registrants from 1 November 2025, all new voluntary GST registrants from 1 April 2026, and all remaining GST-registered businesses in waves from April 2028 through April 2031. B2B e-invoicing itself is not universally mandated; the obligation is specifically to transmit invoice data to IRAS through InvoiceNow-Ready Solutions using the Peppol PINT SG format.

name: Sint Maarten
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Tax Administration Sint Maarten (Inspectorate of Taxes)
summary: Sint Maarten operates its own independent tax administration established on 10 October 2010, when the island became a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. No e-invoicing mandate, structured format requirement, or credible legislative programme has been identified in the available sources. Invoicing obligations exist within the Turnover Tax (TOT) framework, but no electronic invoice format or clearance model has been introduced.

name: Slovakia
keyDate: Mandatory B2B from 1 Jan 2027; voluntary pilot from Q2 2026
model: 5-corner Peppol CTC with certified Digital Postmen
format: EN 16931 / Peppol BIS (UBL 2.1 or CII D16B)
authority: Financial Administration of the Slovak Republic (Finančná správa SR)
summary: Slovakia has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate via the IS EFA platform and is introducing a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and real-time reporting obligation from 1 January 2027, with a proposed penalty-free grace period through 31 March 2027. The B2B system is built on a 5-corner Peppol network operated by accredited Digital Postmen, requiring EN 16931-compliant structured XML invoices; a voluntary pilot opened from Q2 2026. Reporting of purchase invoices has been proposed to be deferred to 1 July 2030, aligned with the EU ViDA initiative.

name: Slovenia
keyDate: B2G e-invoicing mandatory since 2015; ZIERDED law promulgated 31 October 2025 sets B2B e-invoicing mandate at 1 January 2028 (definitive date, postponed from an earlier Jan 2027 draft target); no e-reporting requirement
model: Decentralized Continuous Control and Exchange Model (DCTCE) — direct structured exchange between parties, no real-time reporting to FURS
format: e-SLOG 2.0, Peppol BIS 3.0, UBL 2.1, or EN 16931 CII
authority: Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia (FURS); Ministry of Finance
summary: Slovenia has required B2G e-invoicing via the e-SLOG standard since 2015, processed through the Public Payments Administration (UJP/PPA). On 23 October 2025, Slovenia's National Assembly adopted the Act on the Exchange of Electronic Invoices and Other Electronic Documents (ZIERDED), promulgated by the President on 31 October 2025, establishing 1 January 2028 as the definitive B2B e-invoicing mandate date — a further postponement from an earlier draft target of 1 January 2027 (itself already postponed from initial April/July 2026 proposals). The final law adopted a Decentralized Continuous Control and Exchange Model (DCTCE) and definitively removed an earlier real-time e-reporting requirement that had been part of draft versions of the bill. Accepted formats are the national e-SLOG 2.0 standard, Peppol BIS 3.0, UBL 2.1, or EN 16931 CII.

name: South Africa
keyDate: SARS has confirmed mandatory e-invoicing targeted for 2028 under the VAT Modernisation Project; Draft Tax Administration Laws Amendment Bill (TALAB) published for comment 16 August-12 September 2025; large taxpayers first, phased over five years from an initial 2023 proposal
model: Anticipated decentralised Five-Corner Model (Peppol-style, via approved/certified service providers) — not yet legislated in final form
format: TBC — structured electronic format (e.g. XML); PINT (Peppol International Invoice) under consideration; final technical specification not yet published
authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); National Treasury
summary: South Africa does not yet mandate e-invoicing. Under its VAT Modernisation Project, SARS published a discussion paper in September 2023 proposing a shift to real-time VAT reporting (invoice/payment data submitted within 24 hours, eventually reduced to 6 then 1 hour, using submitted data to pre-populate VAT returns, phased over five years starting with large taxpayers). SARS and National Treasury published the Draft Tax Administration Laws Amendment Bill (TALAB) for public comment from 16 August to 12 September 2025, laying the legal groundwork for mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting. SARS has since confirmed a target of 2028 for mandatory e-invoicing, with South Africa reportedly leaning toward a decentralised Five-Corner (Peppol-style) model similar to France, Singapore and Belgium, potentially using the PINT (Peppol International Invoice) format. Since 1 April 2025, invoice data has also been required on electronic customs declarations, and companies wishing to use EDI-based invoicing today still need prior SARS/National Treasury authorisation.

name: South Korea
keyDate: Mandatory for all corporate taxpayers since 1 Jan 2011; individual entrepreneur threshold progressively reduced, currently 80 million KRW annual supply value (from Jul 2024), further reduced Jul 2025
format: e-Tax Invoice, standardised XML, PKI digital signature
summary: South Korea's e-Tax Invoice (전자세금계산서) system, one of the world's earliest e-invoicing mandates, has required all corporate taxpayers to issue and transmit electronic tax invoices to the NTS Hometax platform within one day of issuance since 1 January 2011. The mandate has progressively extended to individual entrepreneurs (sole proprietors) via a steadily-lowered annual turnover threshold, currently 80 million KRW as of July 2024, with a further reduction from July 2025. Invoices must be PKI-digitally-signed XML, archived for 5 years; late or missing transmission triggers automatic penalties, typically 0.5% of the supply value.

summary: Spain has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate in place since January 2015, requiring structured Facturae invoices via the FACe platform. The B2B mandate under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) was given legal force by Royal Decree 238/2026, published in March 2026, with a draft Ministerial Order setting an expected entry-into-force date of 1 October 2026 that would trigger compliance deadlines of 1 October 2027 for large businesses and 1 October 2028 for all remaining in-scope taxpayers. The Spain 2025 EC Country Sheet carries a NO VERIFICATION status, so the B2B mandate fields in that source have not been officially validated by Spanish national representatives.

name: Sri Lanka
keyDate: National e-Invoicing System announced in Budget 2026; IRD Notice SEC/PN/VAT/2026-03 confirms pilot (export-oriented enterprises, e.g. garment/tea sectors) with tea brokers transmitting via WEB API from 1 May 2026; full WEB API integration for Phase 1 expected by end of 2026; Phase 2 (all VAT-registered persons) and a later POS-based B2C phase to follow
model: E-reporting via secure WEB API — real-time transmission of VAT invoice data from taxpayers' ERP systems to the Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS)
format: Structured VAT schedule data (Schedule 01 output tax, Schedule 04 credit/debit notes, Schedule 07 zero-rated supplies) transmitted via ERP-to-RAMIS Web API integration
authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Department of Inland Revenue
summary: Sri Lanka's Budget 2026 introduced a National e-Invoicing System, moving the country from a study phase to active implementation. The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) issued Notice SEC/PN/VAT/2026-03 confirming a Web API-based system enabling real-time transmission of VAT invoice data from taxpayers' ERP systems directly to the Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS). The rollout began with a pilot phase involving selected VAT-registered exporters that upgraded their ERP systems for API integration — garment and tea export entities are already connected, and tea brokers began transmitting invoice, credit note, and debit note records to RAMIS from 1 May 2026. Full Web API integration for this first phase is expected by end of 2026. The system automatically transmits Schedule 01 (output tax, including exempt supplies), Schedule 04 (credit/debit notes), and Schedule 07 (zero-rated supplies) — and businesses submitting via the API no longer need to also upload the same records manually via Excel or the RAMIS e-Service interface. Phase 2 will extend the system to all VAT-registered persons, with a final stage extending e-invoicing to B2C transactions via Point-of-Sale (POS) systems.

summary: Sudan's Taxation Chamber officially launched an electronic invoice system starting in May 2026, confirmed directly on the Chamber's own site (tax.gov.sd) as one of its active computing projects alongside core-system digitisation, an e-portal, and infrastructure/network build-out. Under the system, taxpayers generate invoices electronically and the invoice information is transmitted in real time to the Tax Authority, then distributed to taxpayer records in the core system. The Secretary-General of the Tax Chamber confirmed an agreement with the Ministry of Finance on a timetable to fully computerize the system by the end of 2026, with an initial target of reaching 2,000 taxpayers under the electronic invoicing system — indicating a phased rollout from a launched base rather than a universal, fully-enforced mandate.

authority: Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten), Svalbard Tax Office
summary: Svalbard and Jan Mayen have no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme. Svalbard operates under its own simplified flat-tax regime with no VAT, administered by the Svalbard Tax Office under rules distinct from mainland Norway; Jan Mayen applies mainland Norwegian tax rates but has no permanent population. The mainland Norwegian B2B e-invoicing mandate announced for 1 January 2027 applies to entities subject to Norwegian bookkeeping requirements on the mainland and does not extend to Svalbard or Jan Mayen.

name: Sweden
keyDate: B2G live since 2019; B2B inquiry due by Nov 2027
authority: Skatteverket / DIGG (Peppol authority transferring to Upphandlingsmyndigheten from Jul 2026)
summary: Sweden has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate covering all public procurement contracts, with suppliers required to issue EN 16931-compliant invoices and all contracting authorities required to receive them via the Peppol network since 2019. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary but is widely practised. A formal government inquiry launched in February 2026 will assess whether domestic B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting requirements should be introduced, with findings due no later than November 2027.

name: Switzerland
keyDate: B2G e-invoicing mandatory since 1 January 2016 for federal contracts ≥ CHF 5,000; B2B and B2C e-invoicing remain voluntary as of 2026, with no domestic B2B mandate planned — Swiss exporters are instead being pulled into structured invoicing indirectly by France's (from 1 September 2026) and Germany's (from 2027) mandates
model: B2G: pre-clearance-style submission to the Federal Tax Administration via certified providers (no central government portal). B2B/B2C: voluntary, no clearance model
format: SwissDIGIN (Swiss standard); ZUGFeRD/Factur-X (hybrid format) recommended; UBL XML, eCH-011, and Peppol BIS also accepted; QR-bill mandatory for payment slips
summary: Switzerland has no domestic B2B or B2C e-invoicing mandate; both remain fully voluntary, and Swiss law's only standing structured-invoicing obligation is for B2G transactions: since 1 January 2016, suppliers billing the federal administration for contracts of CHF 5,000 or more must submit electronic invoices, via certified service providers rather than a central government portal. Switzerland's own recommended standard is SwissDIGIN, with the hybrid ZUGFeRD/Factur-X format also recommended and UBL XML, eCH-011, and Peppol BIS accepted. Separately, and distinct from invoice-level e-invoicing, the QR-bill is the mandatory format for Swiss payment slips (replacing the old payment slip), continuing to evolve technically (structured-address-only requirement from 21 November 2025, implementation guidelines version 2.4). As of 2026, no domestic B2B mandate is planned, but Swiss exporters selling into the EU are being pulled toward structured invoicing indirectly, since France requires structured B2B e-invoicing from 1 September 2026 and Germany from 2027 — EU customers will increasingly refuse PDF invoices regardless of Swiss domestic law.

name: Syria
keyDate: In March 2026, Syria's tax authority discussed reforms covering a unified income tax, sales tax, real-estate sales tax and stamp duty, together with electronic invoicing and electronic payment; in April 2026, a proposed invoicing platform linking companies to the Ministry of Finance through the tax number and commercial register was presented — no enacted law, technical specification, or implementation date exists
model: Not yet confirmed — proposed platform would link companies to the Ministry of Finance via tax number and commercial register
format: Not yet confirmed in sources reviewed
authority: Syrian Ministry of Finance / General Commission for Taxes and Fees
summary: Syria has no enacted e-invoicing system, but there is genuine, recent evidence of active government discussion and proposal. In March 2026, Syria's tax authority discussed a package of reforms including a unified income tax, sales tax, real-estate sales tax, stamp duty, electronic invoicing, and electronic payment; in April 2026, a proposed invoicing platform linking companies to the Ministry of Finance via their tax number and commercial register was presented. This is distinct from vendor marketing pages (such as tax2gov's 'STA E-Invoicing API' page) which speculatively describe what a future system 'would' look like while explicitly confirming 'the Syrian Tax Authority (STA) has no formal e-invoicing system as of 2025 due to ongoing instability.' Given the genuine but very recent and unformalised nature of the April 2026 proposal, this is classified as 'proposed' rather than 'announced' or 'none'.

name: Taiwan
keyDate: eGUI mandatory for all taxpayers since 2018-2021 rollout; MIG 4.0 XML standard mandatory since 1 January 2024 (MIG 3.1/3.2 usable only through 31 Dec 2025); Electronic Invoice Allowance Note (EIAN) reporting rules effective 1 January 2025, fully enforced since 30 June 2025
model: Government platform (electronic Government Uniform Invoice — eGUI), real-time/near-real-time digital reporting
format: eGUI XML (MIG 4.0 since 1 Jan 2024, superseding MIG 3.1/3.2.1), plus a QR-coded PDF
authority: Ministry of Finance (MOF), National Taxation Bureau of Taipei
summary: Taiwan's electronic Government Uniform Invoice (eGUI) scheme has roots in a 2006 standardisation programme; the Ministry of Finance imposed mandatory e-invoicing via gradual implementation from 2018, extending to all taxpayers by January 2021 (foreign and national companies alike), operated through the MOF's Electronic Invoicing Platform. The technical standard was upgraded to MIG 4.0 XML, mandatory from 1 January 2024 (older MIG 3.1/3.2 versions usable only through 31 December 2025). Since 1 January 2025, new rules require sellers to issue and upload an Electronic Invoice Allowance Note (EIAN) for returns, withdrawals, or agreed discounts, with strict upload deadlines (2 days for B2C, 7 days for B2B from the day after issuance); a transitional period ended 30 June 2025, after which full enforcement began, with penalties of NT$1,500-15,000 for late or inaccurate uploads.

name: Tajikistan
keyDate: Electronic VAT invoices are accepted and can be uploaded to a taxpayer's electronic cabinet with the Tax Committee, but are not confirmed mandatory; the Tax Committee has broadly digitalised tax administration (40+ digital services)
model: Not confirmed as a clearance or CTC model — electronic copies of VAT invoices may be annexed to VAT returns or uploaded as registers of accepted/issued invoices via the taxpayer's electronic cabinet
authority: Tax Committee of the Republic of Tajikistan
summary: Tajikistan's Tax Committee has broadly digitalised tax administration — every taxpayer has a personal electronic cabinet, and the Committee has developed 40+ digital tax services including electronic document circulation. Electronic VAT invoices are explicitly accepted (hard copy or electronic copies may be annexed to VAT returns or uploaded as registers of accepted/issued invoices), but a dedicated web search found electronic invoicing is 'not mandatory' — businesses may use it to reduce administrative burden, but paper remains valid. This conflicts with a pre-existing, less-detailed classification in the codebase's static seed data (status 'live', 'required for VAT payers') — given the direct contradiction between sources, this is classified as 'voluntary' as the better-supported middle ground, with the conflict explicitly flagged rather than resolved unilaterally.

name: Tanzania
keyDate: EFD Phase 1 (VAT-registered traders) since 2010; Phase 2 (non-VAT traders above TZS 11m) since 2013; VFD software alternative since 2020; Protocol 2.1 mandatory since 6 January 2021; pre-clearance CTC migration proposed in the 2025/26 Budget (no firm statutory date yet)
model: Fiscal-device model (EFD/VFD) with mandatory real-time transmission to the Electronic Fiscal Device Management System (EFDMS); migrating toward a token-based pre-clearance (CTC) model, not yet in force
format: Bespoke TRA EFDMS XML schema (SHA1-with-RSA signed) — no Peppol, EN 16931, or UBL alignment
authority: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) — Mainland; Zanzibar Revenue Authority (ZRA) operates a separate VFMS regime for Zanzibar
summary: Tanzania has operated mandatory fiscalisation since 2010, when Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs) became mandatory for VAT-registered traders (Phase 1); this extended to non-VAT traders above TZS 11 million turnover in 2013 (Phase 2). A software-based Virtual Fiscal Device (VFD) alternative became available in 2020, and all devices were required to run Protocol 2.1 (enabling input-VAT verification codes) from 6 January 2021. Every fiscal receipt is signed on-device and transmitted in real time to the central EFDMS using a bespoke TRA XML schema — not Peppol, EN 16931, or UBL. The 2025/26 Budget proposed deeper EFDMS integration and a pre-clearance step, but this has no firm statutory effective date yet. Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar operate separate regimes: Zanzibar has its own Virtual Fiscal Management System (VFMS) under the Zanzibar Revenue Authority (ZRA), with different VAT rates. Finance Act 2024 updated EFD penalties (now up to TZS 4,000,000 and/or 3 years' imprisonment for failure to issue/use an EFD), and Finance Act 2025 introduced VAT withholding and a reduced 16% VAT rate for electronically-paid B2C supplies from September 2025.

name: Togo

summary: Togo's 2026 Finance Law (Law No. 2025-002), approved by the National Assembly on 29 December 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, introduces a certified electronic invoicing obligation for B2B VAT transactions and, notably, in cases where a taxable person requests advance payment. Certified e-invoices must be created, transmitted, received, and stored electronically, regardless of the technology used, provided they comply with legal requirements. The Office Togolais des Recettes (OTR) will set up or approve e-invoicing platform(s) and collect transaction data electronically, with implementation details and a specific rollout timeline to be defined by the finance minister's implementing regulations — not yet published as of this dossier. Until the new system is implemented, standardised paper invoices remain in use. This builds on a longer-standing context in which electronic invoicing has been legally equivalent to paper invoicing in Togo since 2018, though used only voluntarily to date.

summary: Trinidad and Tobago's Inland Revenue Division (IRD) is in an early planning phase for a national e-invoicing programme as part of broader tax administration modernisation, but no binding mandatory framework exists. References to digital invoicing capability have appeared in recent Budget Statements and the IRD's strategic transformation agenda, with the proposed Trinidad and Tobago Revenue Authority (TTRA) reform — legislation for which passed in January 2022 — framing e-invoicing as a longer-term capability. As of early 2026, voluntary digital invoicing is permitted, and VAT continues to operate through traditional return-filing channels under the VAT Act via the IRD's existing e-Tax online portal (for filing returns, not structured e-invoicing). No specific technical format, platform, or implementation timeline had been published as of the sources reviewed.

authority: DGI (Direction Générale des Impôts) / TTN (Tunisie TradeNet)
summary: Tunisia's El Fatoora e-invoicing platform, operated via Tunisie TradeNet (TTN) under DGI oversight, is currently mandatory for B2G transactions (large enterprises overseen by the Large Enterprises Directorate) and for B2B transactions in the medicines and fuel supply chains (retail excluded). A draft 2026 Finance Law, published 14 October 2025, proposes extending mandatory e-invoicing to all service transactions from 1 January 2026 — a significant scope expansion — but the sources reviewed explicitly describe this as a draft/proposal pending official publication, not yet confirmed adopted. A penalty framework for non-compliance has applied since 1 July 2025.

Both systems are administered by GİB and use the UBL-TR XML format with mandatory digital signatures. Thresholds have been progressively lowered since 2014, with the general e-Fatura threshold standing at TRY 3 million annual gross sales and sector-specific thresholds as low as TRY 500,000 for e-commerce, real estate, motor vehicles, construction, and intermediary sectors.

summary: Uganda operates the Electronic Fiscal Receipting and Invoicing Solution (EFRIS), administered by the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) under the Tax Procedures Code Act (Cap. 343) and the Tax Procedures Code (Electronic Invoicing and Receipting) Regulations, S.I. No. 82 of 2020. Mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers since 1 January 2021, the mandate was significantly expanded from 1 July 2025 — per General Notice No. 2218 of 2025 — to cover twelve additional business sectors, including certain non-VAT-registered entities operating in designated industries. Invoices generated via ERP system-to-system connection, client application, the URA web portal, or USSD are encrypted, transmitted to EFRIS, validated in real time, and returned with a QR code, verification code, invoice identification number and fiscal document number before being issued to the customer.

name: Ukraine
keyDate: B2G mandatory since 2011; URTI/ERPN registration for B2B/B2C above UAH 1m turnover since 2015; full VAT invoice digitisation since 2018; SAF-T mandatory for large taxpayers from 1 January 2025, all VAT-registered taxpayers from 1 January 2027
model: Clearance-style registration — VAT invoices must be registered in the Unified Register of Tax Invoices (URTI/ERPN) before/at issuance to grant input VAT credit
format: National XML, registered via URTI/ERPN; SAF-T reports in standard XML format
summary: Ukraine has progressively built one of the longer-standing continuous-transaction-control regimes in the region. B2G e-invoicing became mandatory in 2011. The Unified Register of Tax Invoices (URTI, also referred to as ERPN) was introduced in 2015, effectively mandating e-invoicing for B2B/B2C transactions once a supplier's turnover exceeds UAH 1 million. Full VAT invoice digitisation followed in 2018: all VAT-registered taxpayers must issue tax invoices electronically and register them with the tax authority before or at the time of issuing them to customers. A COVID/war-driven moratorium on fines ran from March 2020 through 26 May 2022, with a grace period to 15 July 2022 to register February-May 2022 backlogged invoices without penalty. Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T) reporting began as an optional pilot in 2023, becomes mandatory for large taxpayers from 1 January 2025 (annual filing plus on-demand submission within 2 business days of an audit request), and extends to all VAT-registered taxpayers from 1 January 2027. Ukraine does not currently provide pre-filled VAT returns despite receiving invoice data in real time — the State Tax Service uses e-invoice data to cross-check taxpayer-submitted declarations after the fact.

name: United Arab Emirates
keyDate: Mandatory B2B/B2G from Jan 2027 (large businesses); all VAT-registered from Jul 2027
authority: Ministry of Finance / Federal Tax Authority (FTA)
summary: The UAE is implementing a phased mandatory e-invoicing programme supervised jointly by the Ministry of Finance and the Federal Tax Authority. A voluntary pilot phase opened in July 2026, with mandatory compliance for large businesses from 1 January 2027 and for all other VAT-registered businesses from 1 July 2027. The framework adopts a Peppol-based five-corner model and requires invoices in structured XML format aligned with PINT AE standards, transmitted through FTA-accredited service providers.

name: United Kingdom
keyDate: Mandatory B2B/B2G e-invoicing confirmed from 1 April 2029 (Autumn Budget 2025); implementation roadmap due at Budget 2026
model: Interoperable, Peppol-based network (confirmed Feb 2026); full CTC model details pending Budget 2026
format: TBC — Peppol confirmed as the interoperability layer; the specific invoice document standard has not yet been published
summary: The UK's 2025 public consultation on e-invoicing (HMRC and the Department for Business and Trade, closed May 2025) resulted in a confirmed decision at the Autumn Budget 2025 (November 2025): e-invoicing for all VAT invoices, covering B2B and B2G, will be mandatory from 1 April 2029. Real-time reporting to HMRC is not included, at least initially. HMRC's 2026 'Tax Update 2026: Simplification, Modernisation and Fairness' policy paper confirmed Peppol as the core interoperability network. A detailed implementation roadmap is due at Budget 2026. NHS suppliers already use Peppol-based e-invoicing today (in force since 2019); MTD for VAT digital reporting has applied to businesses over £10,000 turnover since April 2023.

name: United States
keyDate: No federal mandate; voluntary market framework in operation
authority: No single federal authority; Digital Business Networks Alliance (DBNAlliance) governs the voluntary exchange network
summary: The United States has no federal e-invoicing mandate, a position unchanged as of mid-2026, primarily because there is no national VAT or GST system that would drive a clearance-style requirement. The Digital Business Networks Alliance, established by participants in the Business Payments Coalition E-invoice Exchange Market Pilot (which began in 2023), operates a voluntary four-corner exchange network modelled loosely on Peppol. E-invoicing developments at the subnational level, such as California's requirement for state contractors to use Cal eProcure, remain state-specific and do not constitute a national mandate.

name: Uruguay
keyDate: Phased since 1 August 2012 (largest taxpayers); ~98% coverage by late 2024; compulsory for all VAT payers including small businesses (IVA mínimo) from 1 January 2025
format: e-CFE XML (Comprobante Fiscal Electrónico), CAE authorisation code
summary: Uruguay was an early Latin American mover on e-invoicing: DGI's e-CFE (Comprobante Fiscal Electrónico) system began with the largest taxpayers on 1 August 2012 and phased in over more than a decade, reaching roughly 98% of invoices nationwide by late 2024. Rather than a post-implementation grace period, Uruguay managed the rollout through gradual phase-in and deadline extensions, with the final push to end-2024 acting as a de facto grace period; full enforcement for all VAT payers, including small businesses (IVA mínimo) and independent professionals, began 1 January 2025. Every e-CFE must be digitally signed and authorised by DGI in real time via a unique CAE code before it carries legal effect.

name: Uzbekistan
keyDate: Mandatory for all legal entities since 1 January 2020 (voluntary from 1 July 2019) via Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 522 (2019); AI-based real-time risk-scoring control layer moved to production 1 January 2026
model: Clearance — structured XML invoice transmitted in real time to the State Tax Committee via Soliq.uz for clearance, then routed to the buyer through the platform
summary: Uzbekistan mandates electronic invoicing through the Soliq.uz platform operated by the State Tax Committee, anchored in Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 522 (2019). E-invoicing was voluntary from 1 July 2019 and became mandatory for all legal entities from 1 January 2020, regardless of VAT registration status — paper invoices are not legally valid for in-scope transactions. Every invoice is issued in structured XML, transmitted in real time to the State Tax Committee for clearance, and routed to the buyer through the platform. From 1 January 2026, the system gained a new AI-based real-time risk-scoring control layer, piloted since mid-2025 and formalised via November 2025 Ministry of Economy amendments to the Tax Code under a Presidential Decree: invoices are automatically colour-classified by risk, and VAT credit on high-risk ("red") invoices is withheld from the buyer until the corresponding VAT has actually been remitted to the state budget.

name: Vanuatu
keyDate: VAT Monitoring System (VSMS), powered by Data Tech International's TaxCore, with rollout planned between August 2025 and January 2026 — that window has elapsed as of this dossier (10 August 2026), though independent confirmation of full completion was not found
model: Real-time VAT/fiscal monitoring via TaxCore-based Value Added Tax Monitoring System (VSMS)
format: Not detailed in sources reviewed beyond the TaxCore platform
authority: Vanuatu Ministry of Finance, Inland Revenue (Customs and Inland Revenue)
summary: Vanuatu is implementing a VAT Monitoring System (VSMS) powered by Data Tech International's TaxCore platform, led by Collins Gesa, Deputy Director of Inland Revenue at Vanuatu's Ministry of Finance, to digitize tax monitoring and improve VAT collection. The rollout was planned for August 2025 through January 2026, customized to Vanuatu's local needs and drawing on Data Tech International's prior implementation experience in Fiji and Samoa. As of this dossier's date (10 August 2026), that planned rollout window has fully elapsed, but no source reviewed independently confirms completion or full nationwide operation, so this is classified as 'phasing' rather than confirmed 'live'.

name: Vatican City
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Amministrazione del Patrimonio della Sede Apostolica (APSA)
summary: Vatican City operates its own independent tax administration, distinct from any parent/host state, but no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been found. Sovereign city-state with its own administration and negligible commercial economy relative to a typical country. No e-invoicing mandate or need for one was found. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Venezuela
keyDate: Digital fiscal invoicing mandatory; Administrative Ruling SNAT/2024/000102 issued late 2024, implementation anticipated March 2025
format: National (SENIAT-specified formats for fiscal machines and digital invoicing systems)
summary: Venezuela operates a mandatory fiscalised invoicing regime administered by SENIAT, under which businesses must use either authorised fiscal machines or SENIAT-approved digital invoicing systems. In late 2024 SENIAT issued Administrative Ruling No. SNAT/2024/000102, which regulates the use of digital media for the issuance of invoices and other tax documentation, with implementation anticipated for March 2025. The ruling covers entities transacting via electronic means or web portals and introduces digital invoicing as an alternative to fiscal machines for qualifying taxpayers.

name: Vietnam
keyDate: Mandatory since 1 July 2022; updated regulations effective 1 June 2025
format: National structured XML, GDT technical standards
summary: Vietnam has mandated structured e-invoicing for essentially all taxpayers since 1 July 2022 under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP, administered by the General Department of Taxation (GDT). E-invoices are either "authenticated" (granted a tax-authority authorisation code before delivery to the buyer, a clearance-style flow) or "unauthenticated" (sent directly by the seller without prior authorisation, for eligible taxpayers). Decree 70/2025/ND-CP and Circular 32/2025, effective 1 June 2025, updated the framework to address practical gaps and align with the amended VAT Law.

name: Wallis & Futuna
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Service des Douanes et Contributions Diverses, Wallis-et-Futuna
summary: Wallis and Futuna is a French overseas collectivity with its own autonomous customs and indirect-tax administration, the Service des Douanes et Contributions Diverses, operating independently from metropolitan France. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been identified for the territory. France's national e-invoicing reform, phasing from September 2026, does not extend to Wallis and Futuna, which lies outside the scope of French VAT law.

name: Western Sahara
keyDate: No mandate
authority: No independent tax administration; Moroccan DGI administers areas under Moroccan control
summary: Western Sahara is a disputed territory with no independent tax administration. The majority of the territory is administered in practice by Morocco's Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI), which is developing its own national e-invoicing reform, but no e-invoicing mandate applies to Western Sahara as a distinct jurisdiction. No independent e-invoicing framework, platform, or legal instrument exists for Western Sahara.

name: Yemen
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Yemen in the sources reviewed. The vendor page explicitly states: 'The Yemen Tax Authority (YTA) ... could lead e-invoicing compliance if implemented, though no formal system exists yet.' YTA's own official site shows only tender notices and general tax administration content, no e-invoicing mention.

name: Zambia
keyDate: Smart Invoice mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers from 1 July 2024 (Statutory Instrument No. 58 of 2023); grace period 1 Jul-30 Sep 2024; penalties for non-compliance from 1 October 2024
model: Software-based real-time reporting — invoice data transmitted via a Virtual Sales Data Controller (VSCD) module to ZRA's Smart Invoice platform, validated with a unique Mark ID and QR code
format: Structured digital format via Smart Invoice / VSCD
summary: Zambia mandates structured electronic invoicing through the Smart Invoice system, introduced by the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) under the Value Added Tax (Electronic Invoicing System) Regulations, Statutory Instrument No. 58 of 2023. Smart Invoice became mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers from 1 July 2024, replacing the previous Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs) regime and expanding coverage beyond VAT and the Insurance Premium Levy to include Sales Tax, Rental Income, Tourist Tax and Local Electricity Consumption Tax. A grace period for onboarding without penalties ran from 1 July to 30 September 2024, with penalties for non-compliance applying from 1 October 2024. Businesses download a Virtual Sales Data Controller (VSCD) module to transmit invoice and inventory data to ZRA in real time; each validated invoice receives a unique Mark ID and QR code.

name: Zimbabwe
keyDate: Mandate active; buyer-detail upgrade deadline May 2025
format: Device/API (no prescribed inter-party format; QR code required on output)
summary: Zimbabwe operates a mandatory fiscalisation regime under which all VAT-registered operators and, more broadly, all taxpayers must transmit invoice data to ZIMRA's Fiscalisation Data Management System in real time via approved hardware devices or a virtual API. Invoices are cleared through the FDMS portal and must carry a verifiable QR code; only fiscalised invoices that comply with Section 20(4) of the VAT Act are accepted for input tax claims. A May 2025 directive extended the obligation to include mandatory transmission of buyer details such as name, address, TIN and VAT registration number.
